articles.title: Bayern coach Vincent Kompany to remain in hospital after training-ground collapse as club reveals recovery timeline with no return date set
articles.summary: Bayern Munich's coach Vincent Kompany remains hospitalized after collapsing during training. The club has provided a recovery timeline, stating he will require weeks to recuperate, with no specific return date set. Health remains the priority as the team prepares for upcoming matches without him.
articles.body: Vincent Kompany is expected to remain in hospital for several more days after collapsing while watching Bayern Munich’s reserve team train, with sporting director Max Eberl confirming the manager is stable but still undergoing medical checks. Bayern have also made clear that the Belgian will be given weeks, rather than days, to recover, as the club prepares for its next matches without setting a return date.Kompany collapsed while watching Bayern’s reserve team trainKompany was taken to hospital on Friday, October 23, after collapsing while watching a training session involving Bayern’s reserve side. The club confirmed shortly afterwards that he had required medical attention and would undergo a thorough examination.“Vincent Kompany had to seek medical treatment on Friday after collapsing during training for FC Bayern's amateurs,” Bayern said in its statement.“The first-team coach had been watching the second team's session. Kompany will undergo a thorough examination in the hospital and remain in medical care. For the time being, his coaching staff will manage training and match operations."The incident came after the 39-year-old had been dealing with a viral infection and a hip injury that affected his mobility. Kompany missed training on Monday and Tuesday, leaving assistants Aaron Danks and Rene Maric to lead preparations for Bayern’s Champions League meeting with Arsenal.He was nevertheless well enough to attend Wednesday’s 2-2 draw against Arsenal from the dugout, having also overseen Bayern’s 6-1 win over RB Leipzig the previous weekend.After the Arsenal match, Kompany told Bild that he had pushed himself too hard while ill.“As a coach, you always want to do everything and accomplish what you can. I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn't listen to my body, so at some point it just said: Stop now!”Max Eberl says Kompany is stable and needs timeBayern sporting director Max Eberl provided a more reassuring update on Saturday, October 24, confirming that Kompany was stable but would remain in hospital for several more days.“The good news is he's stable. I spoke with him last night, with his wife too. It wasn't a nice moment for all of us, he collapsed on the pitch yesterday and will spend a few more days in hospital until everything is checked over. It shows again how health is the most important thing in life - not football. So, all of us send our best well-wishes. We as FC Bayern stand together. The most important thing is that the cause is established and he gets fit again, and can recover in peace."He'll only come back when he's fit. The tests have already yielded some results, but further results are needed to determine exactly what it is and how long it will take for him to recover. He’s in the best hands. The best thing we can do is support him emotionally with energy and love.”Eberl stressed that the club would not rush Kompany back before doctors had established what caused the collapse and how long his recovery would take.Bayern considered postponing their Freiburg matchThe incident also affected Bayern’s reserve players, who witnessed Kompany collapse during their training session. Eberl said the experience had been difficult for the young squad, with some players understandably overwhelmed.“For the U23s, it happened while they were training, so they experienced it first-hand. For 17- and 18-year-old boys, that's quite something – many of them haven’t had to deal with anything negative before. Some things just happen. The boys were a bit overwhelmed; that’s only human.“Thanks to Vilzing and the Bavarian Football Association for being so quick to say: ‘Let’s postpone the match.’ There are more important things than football. These things weigh on us as human beings. The most important thing is that we’re healthy. Everyone looks out for one another; that’s what defines FC Bayern."We’re there for each other and for everyone else who’s affected by this.”Bayern had considered asking the Bundesliga to postpone their trip to Freiburg on Sunday, October 25. Eberl said the club ultimately believed playing and succeeding would be the best outcome for Kompany, while the manager remained in hospital.Kompany’s return will be measured in weeks, not daysEberl made clear that Bayern would give Kompany all the time required to recover, without setting a deadline for his return to work.“We need to find out what the issue is, and then it’s a question of what the recovery time will be. We're not talking in terms of days, but weeks. We’re all clear on that. “And we have such a fantastic coaching staff, led by Vinnie. But our success is down to an outstanding team behind the scenes. There’s absolutely no thought of changing anything. All the guys here are outstanding – and so, in the spirit of Vinnie, which everyone carries within them, we can all tackle the coming weeks."Support has also come from Manchester City, where Kompany spent years as captain before moving into management. The club posted on X: “Everyone at Manchester City is wishing a speedy recovery to our former captain and Club legend, Vincent Kompany,” followed by: “Get well soon, Vinny.”For now, Bayern’s focus remains on Kompany’s health, with further medical results needed before the club can say when its head coach might return.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Philip Rivers Reportedly Potential NC State HC Candidate with Son Gunner Committed to Wolfpack
articles.summary: North Carolina State will reportedly consider former Wolfpack quarterback Philip Rivers for their open football head coach position after firing longtime program leader Dave Doeren on Saturday night, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel.
articles.body:
North Carolina State will reportedly consider former Wolfpack quarterback Philip Rivers for their open football head coach position after firing longtime program leader Dave Doeren on Saturday night, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel.

Rivers has been the head coach at St. Michael Catholic High School in Fairhope, Alabama since 2021. His son, 4-star quarterback Gunner Rivers , is set to enroll at NC State next year.

The 44-year-old Rivers enjoyed a great career at NC State capped by 2003 ACC Player of the Year honors. He played 16 seasons for the San Diego/Los Angeles Chargers (2004-2019), making the Pro Bowl in half of those seasons. Rivers played one more year with the Colts in 2020 before retiring for the first time.

Five years later, Indianapolis called in need of a quarterback to help finish the 2025 season after QB1 Daniel Jones suffered a torn Achilles last December. Rivers made three starts and impressed considering his age and the fact that he hadn't played in the NFL in five years, throwing for 544 yards and four touchdowns.

Rivers remained the St. Michael's head coach and is now leading the team during Gunner's senior season. Rivers is ranked 12th overall among all quarterbacks in the class of 2027, per the latest 247Sports Composite rankings.

Rivers has led St. Michael Catholic to a 49-18 record . The 2024 and 2025 teams reached the Class 4A semifinals in the state playoffs.

He's fared quite well as St. Michael's coach. Obviously, coaching college is a much different and harder beast. Still, Rivers has a tremendous football resume and pedigree that should command respect among players and help him succeed if he takes the job.

As Thamel implied, though, NC State should likely cast a wide net. Still, Rivers would be an intriguing, potentially home run pick.

articles.title: Barcelona - Real Madrid: 'Match-ball' o salvavidas
articles.standfirst: Lamine y Mbappé ocupan el foco a 24 horas del Balón de Oro • Rodri pone el morbo • Fermín ocupará la plaza de Olmo y Camavinga apunta al once de Mourinho
articles.summary: Lamine y Mbappé ocupan el foco a 24 horas del Balón de Oro • Rodri pone el morbo • Fermín ocupará la plaza del lesionado Olmo y Camavinga apunta al once de José Mourinho
articles.body: El primer clásico de la temporada 26-27 llega con reflejos de oro. El premio de France Football, que se otorga mañana, ha marcado la agenda de las dos grandes estrellas de Barça y Madrid, que han presionado de todas las maneras posibles para fortalecer su candidatura al Balón de Oro. La suerte está echada y parece que Harry Kane ha adelantado por la derecha a Lamine Yamal y Kylian Mbappé. En cualquier caso, no hay mejor partido que el de esta noche para demostrar a los gurús que estaban equivocados y para ir cimentando sus candidaturas para próximas campañas. Hay mucho más en juego, claro. Para los dos. El Barça se encuentra con un 'match-ball' seguramente inesperado gracias a la inconsistencia a domicilio del Madrid, que ya ha concedido dos derrotas en salidas complicadas. La renta de seis puntos a favor de los culés les coloca en una situación de privilegio para distanciar aún más al que todos consideran su gran rival por el título. Nueve puntos no son definitivos en octubre, pero habría que ver el efecto de esa desventaja en la casa del rival, más exigido que nunca tras dos temporadas de decepciones. Para el Madrid aplica la lectura inversa. Un triunfo en Barcelona minimizaría un arranque de temporada con tantos brotes verdes como dudas. El equipo llega de ofrecer una buena imagen en los últimos partidos, pero las derrotas ante Betis y Atlético ponen en entredicho su fiabilidad en estadios delicados. Y pocos lo son más que el Camp Nou para el Madrid, que lleva dos cursos sometido al equipo casi redondo de Hansi Flick, una máquina de hacer puntos en la Liga española. Rodri, en el eje El partido también servirá para avivar o acallar el gran debate del pasado verano, el fichaje de Rodri por el Barcelona cuando muchos le habían puesto ya la camiseta blanca. El madrileño ha encajado a la perfección en el engranaje culé, el gran argumento que le decidío a elegir el Barcelona por delante del Madrid. En el Bernabéu son muchos los que creen que el capitán de la selección era la pieza que faltaba para dar pausa y poso a un centro del campo que gusta más del vértigo y las transiciones. El Barça llega más tocado tras la última jornada de Champions, que deparó una visita a la guarida del campeón. En París cosecharon los catalanes la primera derrota de una temporada impecable, en la que puede batir el récord de victorias consecutivas en el arranque del campeonato doméstico. Un triunfo esta noche sería el décimo, superando un registro del Madrid que data de los años 60. Tendrá que hacerlo el Barça sin Eric García ni Dani Olmo, dos bajas de peso en los planes de su entrenador. Gerard Martín y Fermín apuntan a un once en el que, por lo demás, Lamine y Raphinha volverán a ser las referencias ofensivas. Ese rol lo desempeña en el Madrid Mbappé, que sale a gol por partido en este arranque de curso, cargado de presión extra ante la baja de Vinicius. Viene contando en los últimos partidos con la ayuda de Yan Diomande, eficaz en el regate y en el remate, aunque la gran sorpresa puede venir desde el centro del campo. El plan de Mourinho pasa por reforzarlo con Camavinga y Tchouaméni, con Fede Valverde de nuevo en el lateral y Arda en banda derecha. Una apuesta por ganar la batalla en la media, siempre determinante en estos partidos.

articles.title: Athletic - Getafe | Un incendio que apagar
articles.standfirst: Ambos están al borde del descenso
articles.summary: Ambos están al borde del descenso
articles.body: El Athletic recibe al Getafe en San Mamés con la necesidad de reaccionar después de cuatro partidos consecutivos sin ganar. Los rojiblancos regresan ante su afición más de un mes después de su último encuentro como locales, con el objetivo de recuperar sensaciones tras la derrota ante el Levante. Los problemas ofensivos y los errores defensivos del último partido han aumentado la presión sobre el equipo de Edin Terzic, que está igualado a puntos con el conjunto madrileño. En el apartado de bajas, Laporte no estará disponible por sanción mientras que Guruzeta sigue lesionado. Sancet, también entre los ausentes, entra en la última fase de su recuperación. El Getafe visita San Mamés en un momento delicado de la temporada. Tras la goleada recibida en Conference League frente al Lugano, el cuadro dirigido por José Bordalás quiere, en La Catedral, lograr los primeros puntos de la temporada en LaLiga fuera de casa. Para ello, el alicantino seguirá sin poder contar con Orel Mangala y Zaid Romero, por lesión, además de tener la baja de Djené, que vio la roja frente al Rayo Vallecano la pasada semana. El Getafe, un punto por encima del descenso, quiere vencer y no pasar apuros en un exigente año como es el actual, con tres competiciones y un nuevo encuentro este jueves, por Copa del Rey, que hará que el equipo siga sin tener descanso entre semana.

articles.title: Keelon Russell Impresses, Final Box Score Stats, Highlights, Draft Stock from Alabama Win vs. TAMU
articles.summary: Keelon Russell produced the third 300-yard game of his Alabama Crimson Tide career in Saturday's 31-20 win over the Texas A&M Aggies.
articles.body:
Keelon Russell produced the third 300-yard game of his Alabama Crimson Tide career in Saturday's 31-20 win over the Texas A&M Aggies.

Russell was responsible for three of Bama's four touchdowns in the bounce-back win in SEC play.

Russell took over the game in the fourth quarter with a pair of touchdown passes.

The first-year starter hit Marshall Pritchett for the go-ahead score that moved Bama up by four points.

Russell then connected with Kaleb Edwards for his third touchdown pass of the day to finish off the win over the Aggies.

Just over half of Russell's 311 passing yards went to Rico Scott, who led all pass-catchers with 156 yards on six receptions.

Russell got some help from his defense early in the contest. Dijon Lee Jr. kicked off the scoring with an interception return for a touchdown.

Russell's starring role in the fourth quarter made up for the interception and fumble he lost during Saturday's game.

Although he isn't eligible for the 2028 NFL draft, there's already a decent amount of buzz regarding Russell's potential given his play in 2026 and the struggles experienced by many of the class of 2027's top prospects, like Arch Manning.

Russell is now up to 12 touchdown passes and 1,746 passing yards this season. He'll have to wait until November to add to those statistics. Bama is off next week before it heads to Baton Rouge for a massive SEC clash with the LSU Tigers.

articles.title: Minnesota upsets No. 15 Iowa with walk-off field goal for 13-10 win, effectively ending Hawkeyes' Big Ten title hopes
articles.summary: Minnesota regains the Floyd of Rosedale trophy for the first time in three years and effectively ends Iowa's Big Ten title hopes.
articles.body:
Luke Drzewiecki kicked a 46-yard field goal with no time remaining to give Minnesota a 13-10 win over No. 15 Iowa and the Floyd of Rosedale trophy in Minneapolis on Saturday.

Minnesota moved into position for the game-winning kick on a 39-yard pass from Drake Lindsey to Jalen Smith. Lindsey scrambled to avoid a sack by Iowa's Bryce Hawthorne rushing up the middle, then connected with Smith at the 50-yard line. Smith took it an additional 22 yards to the Iowa 28.

The Gophers held a 10-3 lead after beginning the third quarter with a 71-yard drive that lasted nearly seven minutes and ended with a Darius Taylor 1-yard touchdown run.

However, Iowa finally broke through late in the fourth quarter, going 98 yards on three plays. Hawkeyes quarterback Hank Brown first connected with receiver Tony Diaz, who took an short catch and turned it into a 57-yard gain. Two plays later, Brown found Reece Vander Zee on a post route over the middle for a 37-yard touchdown.

Brown took over at quarterback for Jeremy Hecklinski, who was benched for the Hawkeyes' third possession of the second quarter. Hecklinski finished with 62 yards passing, completing 9 of 16 throws with an interception. Brown threw for 136 yards on 11-of-21 passing with 1 TD and 2 INT.

The defeat dropped Iowa to 2-2 in the Big Ten (5-2 overall), effectively ending their chances of competing for the conference championship. The Hawkeyes are tied for eighth in the standings with four other teams, including Oregon , with UCLA and Ohio State atop the conference at 4-0.

On the other side, Minnesota is still alive for a shot at the conference title game at 3-1 (5-2 overall), tied for third place with Northwestern and USC. Lindsey passed for 137 yards, completing 14 of 26 throws.

The Gophers also regain the Floyd of Rosedale trophy in their annual rivalry with Iowa, winning for the first time in three years. Prior to Saturday, the Hawkeyes had won 10 of the past 11 matchups with Minnesota.

Next week, Minnesota visits Indiana (4-1, 7-1), while Iowa hosts Wisconsin (2-1, 4-2).

articles.title: Watch South Carolina Fans Rush Field in Trending Video After Upset Win vs. No. 11 Tennessee
articles.summary: South Carolina fans wasted no time celebrating a Saturday evening upset win over No. 11 Tennessee.
articles.body:
South Carolina fans wasted no time celebrating a Saturday evening upset win over No. 11 Tennessee.

Fans rushed onto the field at Williams-Brice Stadium immediately after Malik Orsan secured a 27-24 win with a 48-yard walk-off field goal.

Tennessee, which had three potential touchdown passes called back in the loss, started out the fourth quarter with a field goal drive that put the Volunteers up by seven points.

South Carolina tied the game as LaNorris Sellers ran in his third touchdown of the night, then strip-sacked Tennessee quarterback George McIntyre on the Vols' final possession to set up the game-winning drive.

This marks a second straight win over a ranked opponent for South Carolina (4-3, 2-3 SEC), which claimed a road win over Florida when the Gators were ranked at No. 16 back on Oct. 10. The Gamecocks will look to ride that momentum into next Saturday's matchup at Oklahoma (4-3, 2-2 SEC).

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Winners and Losers from Week 8
articles.summary: After a Saturday filled with upsets and nonstop chaos, Week 8 provided another fun slate around college football.
articles.body:
After a Saturday filled with upsets and nonstop chaos, Week 8 provided another fun slate around college football.

Texas Tech unceremoniously dropped from the ranks of the unbeaten, and Big 12 rival BYU followed suit.

In prime time, Texas managed to stop its slide against Ole Miss. And the final matchup of the night is a showdown between Houston and Utah—the latter of which will try to avoid the same fate as Tech and BYU.

This piece will be updated throughout Saturday's action.

Sporting a new throwback uniform from the iconic 2001 championship team, Miami put on a performance that properly honored that squad.

Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney, most specifically.

In a 52-23 rout of Pitt, Mensah completed 31-of-37 passes for 386 yards with four touchdowns. Toney shattered a single-game program record with 16 receptions, racing to 194 yards and three scores.

Another few games like this, and both Mensah and Toney may be heading to New York as Heisman Trophy finalists.

Oh, and the No. 1 'Canes are 7-0. Pretty good vibes in Miami right now.

Texas Tech, on the other hand, endured a disastrous day on the road.

Cincinnati turned a couple of first-half takeaways into 10 points, built a 24-6 halftime lead and snatched a 37-24 upset of the Red Raiders.

The biggest issue for Tech was a disappearing run defense, which entered the game ranked fifth nationally in yards allowed per game at 82.0. Cincy more than tripled that average with 255 yards on the ground.

One loss doesn't wreck the Red Raiders' title aspirations, and their remaining schedule is favorable after a clash with Arizona next Saturday.

But they're officially in must-win territory the rest of the way.

We could complain about Indiana's offense no-showing. It'd be easy to dwell on Michigan's horrendous year on that side of the ball, too.

These defenses, though, folks—they were stellar.

Michigan locked down IU quarterback Josh Hoover, who mustered an 8-of-18 line for 81 yards with an interception. Indiana also struggled on the ground for a third straight game, managing 131 rushing yards on only 3.7 per carry.

But the Hoosiers survived thanks to their own defense, one that yielded 224 yards in a 13-6 overtime win. They generated 10 tackles for loss, two takeaways and sealed the victory with a turnover on downs in OT.

Michigan has a terrible problem on offense. Indiana has serious questions to address after a few unimpressive games.

Nevertheless, we should not lose sight of the excellence from these defenses.

Unranked Teams Cause Chaos in Rankings 📊

Entering the campaign, Oregon was a popular championship pick. I believed in the Ducks. You, specifically, may have doubted them, but a whole lot of yous out there had similarly high expectations.

Even before Dante Moore's concussion, the Ducks were struggling. They trailed Boise State by 10 points in the opener and lost at Oklahoma State. The earliest returns weren't necessarily fantastic.

This, though—a 21-10 loss at Illinois—is a nightmare for a program with a handsomely paid, highly experienced roster. Oregon fell to 4-3 and is effectively out of the College Football Playoff discussion. What seemed like a showdown at Ohio State to begin November has become just another game on the calendar.

Heck, Northwestern might beat Oregon in Eugene next Saturday. That's not a sentence we expected to type in 2026.

To be perfectly honest, I thought Shane Beamer—in his sixth year with the Gamecocks—was going to get fired a few weeks ago.

South Carolina lost to Mississippi State, then suffered a 49-18 blowout at the hands of Alabama, then squandered a 17-0 lead in an overtime loss to Kentucky. Toss in a meltdown that led to a suspension for star defender Dylan Stewart, and it seemed a change was inevitable.

Back-to-back upsets of Florida and Tennessee have calmed the water pounding Beamer's once-sinking ship. LaNorris Sellers accounted for 306 yards and three touchdowns in Saturday's 27-24 win over Tennessee.

Beamer's job security is still tenuous—pitchforks may appear if South Carolina loses to Arkansas, for example—but this hot seat is bearable.

Six teams carried a perfect record into Week 8. Three are gone.

James Madison lost its first game of the season on Thursday night at Appalachian State. Texas Tech fell to Cincinnati on Saturday afternoon, and BYU could not escape this double-overtime clash at UCF.

What a cruel sport, college football. BYU pulled off an epic upset of Notre Dame last weekend and soared to No. 2, the program's best AP ranking since 1984.

BYU remains in the Big 12 and national hunts, but this 39-31 letdown has dimmed the shine on the Cougars' season.

While any loss to Wisconsin would be met with displeasure, USC flat-out stunk. That's the simple, ugly truth.

The running game was a total non-factor. Jayden Maiava threw two interceptions behind a turnstile of an offensive line that surrendered eight tackles for loss (five sacks). Caden Chittenden had a field goal blocked and missed another as the Trojans plodded to a 24-7 loss.

Riley's buyout is not entirely clear, yet it's reportedly around $60 million . That is an obscene, realistically prohibitive number.

It just might not matter anymore. His tenure is a disaster—and getting worse.

Only adding to USC's pain is the success of rival UCLA.

Most hurtfully—and, in the Bruins' case, impressively—this is largely the product of new coach Bob Chesney. The former James Madison boss has propelled the Bruins to a top-10 national ranking and now a 7-0 record for the first time since 2005.

UCLA picked up its latest win with a strong performance against Michigan State. As the defense gave up a meager 156 yards, the Bruins controlled the game on the ground. Anthony Woods scampered for a team-high 112 yards, Wayne Knight chipped in 56, Javion Thomas had 41 and each player scored once.

Perfect, by no means. UCLA started slowly and navigated two first-half fumbles. I'm not rushing to crown the Bruins as a national contender.

The very notion we're having this discussion, however, is the greatest compliment to what Chesney has accomplished in Year 1.

Lucas Carneiro is a phenomenal kicker. I fully understand why Ole Miss coach Pete Golding had faith in his senior specialist.

This decision, nevertheless, was mind-numbing.

Facing a 31-24 deficit at Texas with about 6:20 remaining in the fourth quarter, the Rebels had a 4th-and-10 at the 41-yard line. Rather than keep the offense on the field, Golding chose to have Carneiro attempt a 58-yard field goal.

The worst-case scenario, if he missed? Ole Miss would need a defensive stop and to score a touchdown to win.

The best-case scenario, if he made it? Ole Miss would need a defensive stop and to score a touchdown to win.

Even before we saw the kick, the choice was absurd. And then Texas blocked it.

Boy, did the Longhorns make it interesting again.

They carried a 24-3 advantage into the locker room at halftime...and proceeded to quickly give up 21 straight points. They recovered to take a 34-24 lead...and still needed—after a bizarrely botched onside-kick recovery—a last-second defensive stand to survive Ole Miss.

But they won. Following a week of serious drama, Texas won.

Arch Manning didn't exactly silence his doubters, committing three turnovers in the 34-27 triumph. He also accounted for three touchdowns and made a few tremendous throws. The roller coaster is alive and well.

Mississippi State awaits next Saturday, and trips to Missouri and LSU follow that. Texas has plenty to prove and a long road ahead.

articles.title: No. 2 BYU Upset by UCF as CFB Fans React to Chaotic Game, Top Box Score Stats & AP Poll Prediction
articles.summary: The most chaotic game amid a remarkably dramatic college football season went down in Orlando on Saturday as unranked UCF upset No. 2 (and previously undefeated BYU) 39-31 in double overtime.
articles.body:
The most chaotic game amid a remarkably dramatic college football season went down in Orlando on Saturday as unranked UCF upset No. 2 (and previously undefeated BYU) 39-31 in double overtime.

BYU was a 6.5-point favorite, per FanDuel Sportsbook . The Cougars were also riding the high of a tremendous 28-24 win over previously second-ranked Notre Dame last Saturday.

However, the Knights decided to play spoiler. Here's a look at some notable box score stats.

Losing to an unranked team that sat 3-3 going into the evening should be a tough blow for BYU in the Associated Press poll . The guess is the Cougars will sit in the No. 8-10 range off the strength of their previous record capped by the big Notre Dame win, No. 8 Texas Tech's loss to Cincinnati and No. 11 Tennessee's loss to unranked South Carolina.

UCF and BYU traded punches in regulation. with the Knights' 17-point second quarter being the top highlight until the final sequences in regulation, which had to be seen to be believed.

For starters, UCF had the ball on the BYU 43-yard line with 14 seconds left in the fourth quarter and the score tied at 24. UCF quarterback Keyone Jenkins was taken down, but he was just able to get off an incomplete pass to avoid a sack.

However, on the same play, BYU defensive lineman Keanu Tanuvasa was caught pushing a UCF player's helmeted head down while the two were on the ground, leading to a 15-yard unsportmanlike conduct penalty.

UCF then appeared a bit confused, first spiking the ball and throwing an incomplete pass out of bounds. That led to a 46-yard field goal attempt for the win from kicker Will Stone with 11 seconds left, but his effort got blocked.

Stone recovered the ball behind the line of scrimmage and got his helmet taken off by a BYU player. A flag was thrown, and it appeared UCF could get another chance with two seconds left.

However, after an official review, the flag was picked up, and then there was a 10-second runoff because of the helmet being removed. UCF didn't have a timeout left to stop the clock, and the game went to overtime.

Former NFL referee and NBC Sports rules analyst Terry McAulay said there should not have been a runoff.

Chris Hummer of 247Sports broke it all down via bullet points.

If you're confused about all or even some of that, or simply enthralled by the incredible drama, you're not alone.

Overtime then ensued. Both teams traded touchdowns in the first session. BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier hit wideout Legend Gasker for 28 yards on 3rd-and-13, but Jenkins found wide receiver Josh Derry for 25 yards on the next play. And so the second OT began with the score tied at 31.

UCF's second overtime drive stalled, leading to a short field goal attempt. However, BYU was called for roughing the kicker.

Game analyst Robert Griffin III was not enamored with the call.

UCF took advantage of its second chance when Jenkins found tight end Grayson Brousseau for a four-yard TD. Tyren Hornes then caught a two-point conversion for a 39-31 lead.

BYU got a first down on the UCF eight-yard line, but four straight incomplete passes followed, ending the game.

BYU (6-1 overall, 3-1 Big 12) will now host Arizona State next Saturday. UCF (4-3 overall, 2-2 Big 12) will welcome Baylor into Orlando on Friday evening.

articles.title: UCF outlasts No. 2 BYU in 2OT, notches first top-5 win in program history: 'That's the weirdest end of a game I've ever seen'
articles.summary: Scott Frost's Knights came out on top of a doozy.
articles.body:
UCF wide receiver Tyren Hornes bounced in the Bounce House on Saturday in Orlando. The freshman ricocheted after a hit from BYU linebacker Isaiah Glasker.

After maintaining his balance, Hornes flew down the sideline for a pickup of 56 yards on a third-and-17 that began with him catching a screen pass. The Knights capped that third-quarter drive with a Keyone Jenkins QB sneak that secured a go-ahead touchdown.

It turns out they needed to score one more of those in what proved to be an ethereal conclusion to a matchup that ebbed and flowed more than the mercurial, rainy Florida weather.

Yet No. 2 BYU never brought UCF back down to Earth. Following an end-of-regulation sequence that featured a string of headache-inducing officiating descriptions and a blocked field goal — and then two frames of overtime — the Knights planted an astronomical 39-31 victory in their record book via a fourth-down stop near the goal line.

It's UCF's first-ever win over an AP top-five opponent. The Knights had lost their previous six games in that type of contest.

"Proud of our kids. I'm happy for UCF," said head coach Scott Frost, who is in his second stint leading a program he memorably led to a 13-0 record in 2017.

Frost then added during that on-field postgame interview : "That's the weirdest end of a game I've ever seen."

UCF (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) pulled off the upset of BYU (6-1, 3-1) on a day when another conference titan also fell, with No. 8 Texas Tech losing to unranked Cincinnati earlier on .

The Cougars' defeat comes one week after they knocked off then-No. 2 Notre Dame in game that had its own controversy and that resulted in BYU being ranked inside the top two of the AP Top 25 for the first time since 1984 .

BYU scored on its first series of Saturday's matchup. Quarterback Bear Bachmeier — who caught a touchdown, ran for two more and threw for the game-winning score a week earlier against Notre Dame — tossed a 27-yard TD pass to wideout Kyler Kasper over the middle.

Soon enough, though, the back-and-forth started.

UCF evened things up early in the second quarter when running back Landen Chambers found pay dirt from 2 yards out.

A drop from wide receiver Waden Charles cost the Knights a touchdown on their next drive, but they still came away with a field goal to take a 10-7 lead.

A Bachmeier keeper restored the BYU advantage later on; however, eventually, a deflection-turned-interception set the stage for a UCF touchdown that put Frost's squad up 17-14 heading into halftime. Jenkins, a senior starting his fifth straight game in place of an injured Alonza Barnett III, located Chambers in the flat for a 6-yard score, triggering a paroxysm of excitement .

BYU came out of the break and hopped back into the driver's seat. A 27-yard run from running back Preston Rex that stemmed from an option pitch slingshotted a touchdown drive that saw Bachmeier and Kasper connect on fourth-and-4. Ultimately, running back Sione Moa burrowed in for a 1-yard score.

The Hornes-inspired TD drive swung the pendulum again.

A 47-yard BYU field goal knotted the game at 24 points apiece. As the fourth quarter wore on, UCF nearly took the lead on a 12-play drive that was halted inches short of the end zone by a persistent Cougars goal-line stand.

BYU took over from its own 1-yard line with a bit more than a minute and a half remaining in regulation. Rather than operating with a sense of urgency, Kalani Sitake's team took its time and wound up punting after three run plays.

With that, UCF got another opportunity at a game-winning drive. A 21-yard catch and run by Chambers thrust the Knights into field-goal territory. Frost kept his offense on the field. It looked like the decision might backfire when BYU hit Jenkins.

Fortunately for the Knights, Jenkins got the ball out before he was sacked. Intentional grounding wasn't assessed. Originally, the ruling on the field was a fumble that BYU recovered , except that call was overturned, whereas an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty on the Cougars that play still applied.

In turn, UCF vaulted ahead to the BYU 28-yard line. From there, its potential game-winning 46-yard field goal was blocked.

It looked as though the Knights might get one more shot nevertheless, as the kick occurred on third down and their kicker, Will Stone, recovered the loose ball. But because Stone's helmet came off on the play, a 10-second runoff was triggered, and UCF didn't have a timeout to stop it.

There was also a question of whether there should have been a facemask penalty on the play and how that would have affected the situation.

Longtime rules analyst Terry McAulay chimed in on social media that there shouldn't have actually been a 10-second runoff.

"The clock stopping for the helmet off was not the only reason it stopped," McAulay wrote on X . "It also stopped because it was the end of a legal kick down."

McAulay pointed to the rule book , which states that a 10-second runoff is among the conditions that follow if the helmet coming off is the only reason for stopping the clock (other than due to an injury to the player or their teammate).

The thrills continued into OT, only they shifted back to centering around jaw-dropping plays, not head-turning reviews.

On third-and-13 in the first overtime period, Bachmeier hooked up with wideout Legend Glasker for a 28-yard touchdown. On UCF's first play of OT, Jenkins evaded a sack, bought time and fired a 25-yard TD strike to wide receiver Josh Derry.

In the second overtime period, a roughing the kicker flag on BYU extended a Knights series that was going to end in three points. They ended up scoring eight.

Jenkins, who finished with 293 yards and three touchdowns on 25-of-41 passing, hit tight end Grayson Brousseau for the go-ahead score . Hornes then dove for a catch that converted the necessary 2-point attempt.

Hornes clocked out with six catches and 137 receiving yards in a win that UCF sealed on defense. Bachmeier's fourth-and-goal pass fell incomplete, and Knights faithful bounced — up and down, in complete euphoria.

articles.title: Joan García, un Clásico de triunfos
articles.standfirst: En los dos anteriores cruces ganó la Supercopa de España y celebró LaLiga
articles.summary: En los dos anteriores cruces ganó la Supercopa de España y celebró LaLiga
articles.body: Joan García no sólo cuenta sus Clásicos por triunfos, también son partidos en los que ha acabado festejando títulos. Esta noche, en el Spotify Camp Nou, no hay en juego ningún trofeo, pero sí tres puntos importantes para consolidar la confianza del Barcelona tras la derrota en la Champions League contra el PSG, para sumar la décima, e histórica, victoria consecutiva en LaLiga y para afianzar su liderato en el torneo nacional. El meta catalán se ha medido en cuatro ocasiones al Real Madrid, pero sólo en dos vestía la camiseta azulgrana: en las dos primeras militaba en el Espanyol (un partido lo perdió por 4-1 y el otro lo ganó por 1-0). Se perdió el Clásico de octubre de 2025 por una lesión en el menisco de la rodilla derecha. Aquel encuentro concluyó en triunfo blanco. Los de Xabi Alonso se impusieron en el Santiago Bernabéu por dos goles a uno, y Szczensy fue el cancerbero titular azulgrana del choque. Pero Joan García, de 25 años, sí que jugó la final de la Supercopa de España del pasado mes de enero y también el compromiso del 10 de mayo. En el primer encuentro, el Barcelona se proclamó campeón del torneo disputado en Arabia Saudí. El marcador fue de tres goles a dos. Le superaron Vinicius y Gonzalo. En el segundo compromiso, el equipo de Hansi Flick ganó dos a cero, y certificó, ante su grada, el título de LaLiga. Esta noche, Joan García disputará, por lo tanto, su tercer Clásico, que confía no sólo ganando sino también dejando, de nuevo, su meta a cero. Esta temporada, el portero catalán, que ha recibido 13 goles (seis en la Champions League y siete en LaLiga) ha dejado su arco imbatido en cuatro encuentros entre todas las competiciones. Uno de los grandes retos de Joan García esta noche será frenar a uno de los máximos goleadores del torneo regular: Mbappé. El delantero francés suma nueve goles en estos primeros nueve encuentros. Es el segundo realizador: sólo le supera Raphinha, que ha festejado ¡12! El Clásico le llega al arquero de Sallent en un gran momento. Pese a la goleada encajada en París (el Barça cayó por cuatro tantos a dos), Joan García fue uno de los mejores futbolistas no sólo del Barcelona sino del encuentro: tuvo intervenciones de gran mérito y salvadoras. El conjunto catalán, además, sólo ha recibido nueve dianas en este arranque (el experico no jugó en el Sánchez Pizjuán por unas molestias en la rodilla y el titular culé fue Livakovic) y es uno de los bloques más fuertes defensivamente de LaLiga.

articles.title: Habrá mosaico en el Spotify Camp Nou para el Clásico de la vuelta de Mourinho
articles.standfirst: El estadio culé lucirá un gran ambiente: el club espera hacer récord de taquilla
articles.summary: El estadio culé lucirá un gran ambiente: el club espera hacer récord de taquilla
articles.body: Este domingo se disputa uno de los encuentros más esperados y celebrados del panorama futbolístico mundial: el Clásico entre el Barcelona y el Real Madrid. Estos partidos son una fiesta del balompié y el Spotify Camp Nou se vestirá de gala, como suele ser habitual, para tal señalada ocasión. El Barcelona dará el pistoletazo de salida al encuentro de esta décima jornada de LaLiga con un mosaico. Los detalles del gran tifo que se desplegará en el Spotify Camp Nou no han trascendido, aún, porque la entidad trabaja en el factor sorpresa. La temporada pasada, en el primer cruce contra el Real Madrid tras el retorno por las obras del feudo de Les Corts, en gran parte de la primera y segunda grada se pudo ver el escudo del Barcelona y el lema Força Barça formados por miles de cartulinas de los colores azul y grana. Es la leyenda más habitual en los mosaicos culés. Este domingo, el club catalán también quiere vestir de gala su estadio en un partido importante para el equipo, que quiere confirmar que la derrota en París, en el cruce de Champions League, fue un accidente. Quiere que cuando los de Flick salten al césped del campo azulgrana sientan el calor y apoyo de sus aficionados y comprueben lo especial que es un Clásico. Pero el ambiente del Spotify Camp Nou no sólo será espectacular por el mosaico. También se prevé una excelente entrada. En el Clásico del curso pasado, disputado el 10 de mayo, hubo 62.213 espectadores en las gradas, lo que implicó unos ingresos históricos para el Barcelona. Por la taquilla obtuvo 16,5 millones. Este curso, en la entidad son optimistas y confía en hacer aún más caja. Los precios de las localidades son dinámicos y aumentan con la demanda, que está siendo muy alta.

articles.title: El Clásico de los 649 euros
articles.standfirst: El borde del área, por José Luis Hurtado
articles.summary: El borde del área, por José Luis Hurtado
articles.body: Llega el Clásico, aquello que en tiempos de Di Stéfano y Kubala, de Amancio y Luisito Suárez, y de Butragueño y Guardiola era conocido como el Barcelona-Real Madrid. Los bares se llaman de todo menos bares. Son las modas. Es ahí, en las tripas del evento, donde llega el asombro. Manos arriba, esto es un Clásico. La localidad más barata, -aquí se podría escuchar la sintonía de Curro Jiménez-, para entrar en el Spotify Camp Nou se fijó en 649 euros sin que la Fiscalía haya entrado en el asunto. Por semejante talegada se puede ver El Rey León, la filmografía entera de Los Javis, Los Pedros y Los Fernandos y toda la temporada de un equipo de baloncesto. Si se seca el sudor con billetes lo suyo es comprar la entrada VIP Premium. La puede adquirir en las últimas horas por 2.400 euros. Se lanza con el garfio comercial de que es “full experience” y se vende con prospecto, como el Ibuprofeno. Se señala que con ella se “vive la experiencia completa”. Es decir, por orden: 1) Asiento Premium, “con comodidad y ubicación top”. 2) “Acceso a sala VIP sin colas”. (Es un detallazo). 3) Catering. “Bufet de alta calidad y barra libre”. (Imagino que las gambas bailan break dance y hablan inglés y que te puedes sacudir dos Zacapa con Coca-Cola con los que cuando empieza el partido el resultado te da igual, como en el Carranza de siempre). 4) “Llegada de los jugadores, vive el calentamiento e inicio del partido en el centro del campo“. Lo que no se especifica es si el comprador de la localidad puede tintar el pelo de Lamine Yamal, obtener una consulta gratis con el cirujano de Vini o vivir cinco minutos al lado de la libreta de Mourinho, que estará maquinando una idea para que se pongan los aspersores. LaLiga, antes la Liga en los tiempos de Puskas y Ramallets, podría analizar este asunto. El temido y nunca bien explicado Fair Play financiero pretende evitar que los clubes cometan chanchullos con las cuentas, algo en lo que somos campeones del mundo sin pasar por Infantino, el mejor amigo en el fútbol de Trump, flamante FIFA de la paz. No estaría de más una reunión, de bufet libre o no, para pensar si no se puede colocar un tope al precio de las entradas, al menos a las más baratas. El 4 de noviembre se celebra el Borussia Dortmund-Betis de Champions. La entrada más cara cuesta 95 euros y la más barata, 18. Estos alemanes son unos chiflados Premium.

articles.title: Por fin ha comenzado la salida de Peter Lim del Valencia
articles.summary: Sin ataduras
articles.body: No cantaría victoria ni empezaría a adorar al nuevo “borrego de oro” a ojos cerrados, pero la nota de prensa emitida conjuntamente por el Valencia y Pitchwise, tiene dos conclusiones iniciales: 1.- Lim ha comunicado públicamente que el Valencia está en venta. Que lo quería vender lo sabíamos, pero no se había hecho público y siempre que alguien le preguntaba mentía y decía que no vendía. Incluso a Jorge Mendes se lo ha negado cuando le ha preguntado. 2.- Ha puesto un precio público de salida: 1.250 millones de euros. Aunque en esa cifra hay dos matices. La cifra incluye la deuda del club. ¿Qué cifra de deuda? Eso lo sabrán ellos dos. Me resulta curioso que la nota de prensa del Valencia dice 1.250 millones de euros y la nota de prensa de Pitchwise dice 1.200 millones. No es moco de pavo 50 millones de euros más o menos. A partir de estas dos conclusiones que creo que están claras ya empiezan a no estar tan claras o al menos no explicadas, otra serie de cuestiones; que no significa que no sean ciertas como se han dicho, sino que yo me quiero cuestionar todo y ser muy descreído, debido a los muchos antecedentes, engaños y decepciones que se han sufrido en los últimos años alrededor del Valencia. Básicamente no me creo casi nada, no creo que nadie dé duros a cuatro pesetas y desde luego no voy a ser yo el que empiece como un ingenuo lechón de borrego a amamantar de parabienes, piropos y lindezas a ningún inversor hasta que no vea los hechos y los conozca. Peter Lim también empezó hace 12 años con un préstamo convertible en acciones de 100 millones de euros, que es lo mismo que va a hacer Pitchwise. Y hoy día no hay cosa que desee más la afición del Valencia que Peter Lim salga de la vida del Valencia. Lo desean muchísimo más que trasladarse al Nuevo Estadio. Lo escribo para que los nuevos inversores lo sepan y sepan a donde vienen y con quien se asocian. Es por ello que ayer tarde pregunté a fuentes oficiales y autorizadas de Pitchwise para resolver varias de mis dudas que deben ser las de cualquier valencianista también, si es que se ha aprendido algo del pasado. Pitchwise es una especie de consultoría o empresa de gestión de inversiones, dirigida por dos personas (Ann Rodriguez y Corey Woolfolk) que no son los inversores. Ellos consiguen la confianza de los que tienen dinero para invertirlo en clubes de fútbol. Y lo han conseguido de dos grandes fortunas: los Penner y los Roberts. Los de Walmart y los fundadores del super fondo KKR. Sin entrar en detalles tienen patrimonio y dinero más que de sobra para afrontar la inversión que van a hacer en el Valencia. Es decir no son Dalport ni Mario Alvarado, ambos de funesto recuerdo para el valencianismo. Estas informaciones que detallo a continuación están confirmadas por escrito y oficialmente por Pitchwise. Es muy de agradecer su transparencia, en contraposición del oscurantismo habitual de las fuentes pobres del Valencia que usan la poca información que saben y dan, como mercancía del día a día, para obtener trato amable y favores periodísticos en sus rutinas. Migajas y mini reinos de taifas que pertenecen a otra época arcaica, que se irá acabando. Estos cuatro datos son oficiales según PItchwise: 1.- Los inversores, via Pitchwise, van a pagar entre 460 y 480 millones de euros por el 42% del Valencia. Lo cual me lleva a la primera reflexión: Peter Lim que ha invertido en el Valencia unos 300 millones de euros, va a lograr después de 12 años y de empequeñecer el equipo deportivamente, no sólo recuperar sus 300 millones, sino que de momento obtiene entre 460 y 480 sólo por el 42%. Lo cual me lleva a la primera reflexión: Peter Lim que ha invertido en el Valencia unos 300 millones de euros, va a lograr después de 12 años y de empequeñecer el equipo deportivamente, no sólo recuperar sus 300 millones, sino que de momento obtiene entre 460 y 480 sólo por el 42%. Es decir de momento ya gana 160-180 millones y además le sigue quedando otro 50,5%. Es de estudio y admiración pensando en su bolsillo, porque si le sale bien, le va a ganar a su paso por el Valencia, unos 700 kilos, si vende todo su paquete. Pensando en el club y los 12 años de sufrimiento eso ya se lo dejo a los valencianistas y a los políticos del PP, PSOE y Compromis de Valencia que lo han ayudado a recalificarle de nuevo el viejo Mestalla para que sus acciones valgan más dinero. 2.- Pitchwise de momento van a hacer un préstamo participativo de 100 millones convertible en acciones (en el plazo máximo de un año). Por esa inyección obtendrán un porcentaje inicial que sumado a otros 360-380 millones alcanzarán los 460-480 millones por el 42% acordado. Lim se quedará con algo más del 50.5%. Cito textual “La venta de las acciones de Meriton a Pitchwise ya se ha formalizado. No haríamos el préstamo de 100 millones si no tuviésemos la compra de las acciones firmada". 3.- La operación ya está firmada entre ambas partes y no depende de ningún hito. Es decir no está pendiente de alcanzarse que el equipo juegue la Champions y que el nuevo estadio esté a pleno rendimiento de ingresos para fijar entonces el precio final por el 42%. Yo entiendo que no vale lo mismo el VCF actual que un Valencia hipotético en Champions y con 50 millones más de ingresos por el nuevo estadio. Pero ellos confirman que la operación se cierra ahora en esos términos. 4.- Se ha aceptado una valoración del club de 1.200 millones incluyendo unos 400 millones de deuda (excluida la de CVC que no consideran deuda pura). Detallados los cuatro puntos anteriores, que tengo confirmados por escrito por los inversores, quiero recordar que Peter Lim firmó un contrato de compra-venta del club en el que no tenía obligación contractual de acabar el nuevo Estadio; sin embargo sabía que legalmente tenía que acabarlo antes de 2021 o perdería la calificación urbanística millonaria del solar del actual estadio (viejo Mestalla). E incumplió con el Gobierno Valenciano. Y finalmente lo acabará en junio de 2027, 6 años mas tarde de la obligación que tenía. Traigo este dato a colación porque Valencia está entrenada en incumplimientos y mangarrufas de todo tipo, para estar alerta y descreída. Esperanzada pero con mucha prudencia. Me hago esta pregunta ¿cómo es posible que una empresa o fondo invierta semejante suma de dinero (460-480 millones euros) para no tener al menos el 51% del control del club o l seguridad de que lo tendrá.? Y así lo pregunté a Pitchwise. Esta fue su interesante respuesta: “La influencia y el control no se definen únicamente mediante porcentajes. No entraré en los detalles de los contratos y acuerdos pero Pitchwise no va a estar en el Valencia simplemente para hacer sugerencias y esperar a que Kiat Lim de su visto bueno. Se trata de una auténtica asociación en la que ambas partes deben ponerse de acuerdo a la hora de tomar decisiones. Te pongo un ejemplo que no es exactamente lo mismo pero ilustra: Jim Ratcliffe es propietario minoritario con un 30% del Manchester United pero toma todas las decisiones. Una vez que el acuerdo sea aprobado definitivamente, Pitchwise contará con una presencia constante y activa en Valencia". Me ha generado desconfianza y así lo hago constar, que la nota de prensa del Valencia, nunca habla de hechos consumados o consolidados, no utiliza los tiempos en pasado sino en futuro condicional. De ahí que mis dudas hayan sido insistentes para preguntar a Pitchwise si la operación está cerrada o condicionada a futuro y a hitos. Me insisten que está cerrada salvo que el regulador no lo autorizara (CSD). Siempre pensamos que Lim el día que vendiera su 92% pediría entre 400 y 600 millones de euros. La realidad muestra que le saca 460-480 al 42%, por lo que si hacemos la proporción se acercará a los 1.000 millones cuando venda su otro 50,5%. Repito que olé por él. Lo siguiente es explicar que Lim sigue aquí. Aunque ya no manda él sólo. Lo lógico será que este Fondo de inversores Pitchwise acabe comprando el total del Valencia (el 92% de Lim) y que Lim acabe saliendo de las vidas de los valencianistas. Pero puede ser en un año o puede ser en cinco. También lo pregunté: “De momento vamos a apoyar a los nuevos cambios de ejecutivos que ha habido en el club. Nuestro enfoque actual es por el 42% y trabajar en asociación con Kiat Lim”. En mi opinión la salida de Lim del Valencia ya ha comenzado, porque será Pitchwise o será otro Fondo o inversor, pero Lim está de salida… con los bolsillos llenos y el equipo en la cola otro año más (de momento). Pero el valencianista se tragará el sapo (no tiene otro remedio) de ver como Lim se irá enriquecido, con tal de perderlo de vista. Lo único que dejará aquí que se pueda considerar positivo será un estadio nuevo, de cuyo coste la mitad se ha pagado de decisiones políticas valencianas (150 del solar recalificado de Mestalla + 35 de la torre junto al nuevo estadio). Lo otro que dejará será el nuevo dueño del club y en eso lo único que se puede hacer es rezar para que no sea peor que Lim. Lo que sería muy conveniente es que la sociedad periodística y valencianista no volviera a caer en el error de colmar de piropos anticipados al nuevo propietario y de no convertir la dignidad del aficionado, en una alfombra por la que pise el nuevo dueño…. como ya pasó y pisoteó.

articles.title: Los secretos de la familia que sabe antes que nadie quién gana el Balón de Oro: "Estoy bajo mucha presión"
articles.standfirst: La orfebrería Mellerio es la encargada de componer cada año la pieza más codiciada
articles.summary: La orfebrería Mellerio es la encargada de componer cada año la pieza más codiciada
articles.body: Ganar el Balón de Oro es mucho más que llevarse a casa una pieza única de orfebrería. Pero también es llevarse a casa una pieza única de orfebrería realizada por la casa de alta joyería más antigua del mundo, lo que convierte al vencedor al mismo tiempo en el mejor jugador del planeta y en el poseedor de una joya de la más fina tradición. Situada en el número 9 de la rue de la Paix de París, junto a la lujosísima Place Vendôme, la joyería Mellerio es la encargada de componer el objeto individual más preciado del mundo del fútbol. En vez de cuero y costuras, latón, fuego y cincel. En lugar del logo de una marca deportiva, una inscripción: "Meilleur joueur du monde". Un trabajo artesanal de 100 horas para forjar una llave a la eternidad. El de este año será el Balón de Oro número 70 que salga de la fragua de Mellerio para irse a dormir a casa del mejor jugador del mundo. Y, como el primero, se entregará en Inglaterra. La gala del London Palladium servirá para homenajear a Stanley Matthews, mejor jugador de 1956, que recibió aquel primer galardón que era mucho más pequeño que el actual en un acto íntimo en el ayuntamiento de Blackpool de manos de Gabriel Hanot, el periodista clave en la creación del Balón de Oro. El que se entregue este año, aunque tenga la misma dirección en la partida de nacimiento, es notoriamente distinto a aquel. Y pese a lo que pueda pensar alguno, "no, no es un balón de oro macizo". Lo explica Laure-Isabelle Mellerio, mujer de Laurent, representante de la 14ª generación de la estirpe de los Mellerio, y sucesora de su marido tras su muerte al frente de la joyería. Ella, junto al joyero encargado de cincelar el nombre del ganador en el trofeo, deben guardar un secreto que France Football intenta que no se desvele hasta el momento cumbre de la gala. "Tengo cuatro hijos a los que les encanta el fútbol, así que estoy bajo mucha presión... ¡pero no! Se trata de confiar en la empresa. Mantengo el nombre del ganador en secreto", confesaba a FranceInfo. Todo empieza con dos semiesferas de latón. A base de soplete y manos expertas se va dando forma a lo que después será la forma esférica que todos conocemos. "La pieza se calentará hasta adquirir un tono rojizo parecido al rojo cereza", explica en un vídeo Jean-Pierre Cottet-Dubreuil, orfebre, con la pieza entre las manos. Para unir las dos semiesferas se aplica una soldadura de plata antes después sumergir la pieza en una solución suave con ácido que permite eliminar los restos de soldadura y los retoques finales se dan con lima, antes de dejar pulido el futuro trofeo. A puro cincel y martillo se logran las costuras características de la pelota, que se da un baño para, con ayuda de una corriente eléctrica, depositar oro puro sobre él y darle su acabado final antes de insertarse en una base de pirita, seleccionada y moldeada por los expertos de Mellerio, que supone un toque de distinción para cada poseedor de la joya. "Es esa base de pirita la que hace que cada año el Balón de Oro tenga un peso distinto y que todas las piezas sean únicas. El trofeo terminado pesará entre 10 y 12 kilos aproximadamente. Como estos bloques de pirita varían de un año a otro y de un balón a otro, no hay dos balones que sean iguales. De hecho, si nos fijamos en los de Messi, todos los bloques son diferentes", desvela el orfebre. "Después, se entrega al grabador, que tiene la suerte de conocer antes que nadie el nombre del ganador", cuenta Jean-Pierre Cottet-Dubreuil. Pero tras grabar el nombre del ganador, el año y el logo del trofeo y de France Football, queda un truco final. Si nos fijamos en las fotos de Aitana o de Dembélé en la pasada gala, en el lugar donde unos minutos después ya luce su nombre aparece un pequeño accesorio que esconde el secreto mejor guardado del fútbol, una pequeña chapa para ocultarlo hasta que el elegido lo tenga en sus manos y obtenga la propiedad de una pieza destinada a reyes y reinas. Del fútbol, en este caso. La familia Mellerio emigró en 1515 de su hogar en el valle de Vigezzo, en el norte de Italia, y se estableció en París. Un siglo después de su llegada, como recuerdan en su propia página web, la reina María de Médici les concedió privilegios para ejercer su profesión como recompensa por haber frustrado una conspiración contra su joven hijo Luis XIII, lo que inició una relación con el poder en Francia que se hizo más estrecha en tiempos de María Antonieta, enamorada de las joyas y las pequeñas figuritas que el taller, entonces llamado Mellerio dits Meller, le proporcionaba y que servían de obsequio para las visitas de la consorte en Versalles. En 1815, tras explotar una gran relación con la familia Bonaparte, François Mellerio abrió su tienda en la rue de la Paix, en el mismo lugar en el que hoy se puede envidiar su escaparate. Su clientela siguió creciendo y enamoró a Eugenia de Montijo, emperatriz de Francia como esposa de Napoleón III. Esa relación y las revoluciones europeas de 1848 animaron a la familia de orfebres a abrir una sucursal en Madrid, donde atendió peticiones de Isabel II como la famosa Tiara Mellerio o Tiara de las Conchas, un regalo para su hija Isabel de Borbón, 'La Chata', y que aún luce en el joyero real. La reina Sofía se la prestó en 2007 a la entonces princesa Letizia, que la llevó en una recepción de la visita oficial a España de la presidenta de Filipinas. Además de su cercanía con la alta sociedad, Mellerio también tiene una relación con el deporte que ha convertido a Rafa Nadal en su mejor 'cliente'. O en su mejor 'pieza'. Más allá del Balón de Oro, que fabrica desde 1956, de su taller sale también la Copa de los Mosqueteros desde 1981, aquella que ha mordido el tenista español en 14 ocasiones. Pero los tenistas no tienen la suerte de llevarse a casa una joya como esa. Sólo pueden lucirla unas horas y hacerse fotos con ella con la Torre Eiffel de testigo, antes de que vuelva a su hogar, en la oficina del presidente de la Federación Francesa de Tenis. La única excepción, como no podía ser de otra forma, es Rafa Nadal. Tras ganar por décima vez en Roland Garros en 2017, el torneo decidió obsequiarle con una réplica y permitir, por primera vez, que la Copa de los Mosqueteros saliera de las fronteras de París. A la ilustre nómina de dueños de piezas de Mellerio que componen Rafa Nadal, Leo Messi, Alexia Putellas o la emperatriz Josefina se unirán este lunes dos nuevos miembros, propietarios de una joya salida de un taller que, durante los siglos, ha forjado piezas que son billetes a la inmortalidad.

articles.title: College football winners and losers: Stunning falls from grace by Oregon, Michigan and others show farce of preseason polls
articles.summary: Five of the top 20 teams in the preseason AP poll already have at least three defeats.
articles.body:
The top of the AP Top 25 already looks incredibly different than it did ahead of the season.

Thanks to Oregon's loss at Illinois on Saturday, three teams in the top 10 of the preseason AP poll and five teams that were inside the top 20 have lost at least three games through the first eight weeks of the season. That list includes Oregon, Texas A&M, Oklahoma, Michigan and Penn State.

And with Texas A&M (4-4) losing Saturday, two of those six teams already have four losses.

The Aggies and preseason No. 18 Penn State (3-4) are having seasons so bad that they'd already be out of contention if next year's 24-team playoff was in effect this season.

Oregon's spiral is the most shocking of the six. The Ducks were 12.5-point favorites against the Illini despite missing QB Dante Moore for a third straight game because of his concussion as well as four of the team's top five receivers.

Those are absences that can't be discounted. But Oregon was the No. 2 team entering the season because of the depth of the roster. While the plan was to obviously not count on Dylan Raiola for meaningful snaps in 2026, it was nice to have a two-year starter on the roster to learn from Moore.

Outside of a stellar effort in relief of Moore immediately after he was injured against USC, Raiola has struggled. The Ducks scored a touchdown on their opening drive on Saturday and proceeded to need 89 yards for a 20-yard field goal late in the second quarter.

Minus those two drives, the Ducks averaged under 25 yards over their other 11 possessions.

Given the success Kentucky is having under Will Stein, it's clearer by the week just how important the former Oregon OC was to the infrastructure in Eugene. In Week 2, Oklahoma State's players had already keyed in on stance tendencies exhibited by the Oregon offensive line. And now the Ducks have scored a combined 42 points over their last three games.

The playoff is assuredly out of the question now for Oregon, even with a game at No. 3 Ohio State remaining. Yes, the Buckeyes don't have QB Julian Sayin, but you have to do a lot of mental gymnastics to envision Oregon ending the season on a five-game win streak.

Texas A&M started the season at No. 8 in the AP Top 25 and is now 1-4 in the SEC after a 31-20 loss to No. 13 Alabama. Like Oregon, its offensive coordinator from a year ago got a power conference head coaching job as Collin Klein went back to Kansas State. And, also like Oregon, lack of consistent quarterback play has been an issue.

Marcel Reed has been one of the worst power conference passers in college football. Against the Crimson Tide, he was 14-of-21 passing for 163 yards and threw two interceptions. Reed also fumbled three times, but was lucky to lose just one.

After averaging 6.4 yards a play a year ago, the Aggies' offense is barely above 5 yards a snap in 2026.

Yet both the Oregon offense and the Texas A&M offense look like well-tuned Ferraris compared to what's happening at Michigan. The preseason No. 16 Wolverines are 4-3 despite not allowing more than 20 points in a game all season.

This week, Michigan gave up just one touchdown in a 13-6 overtime loss to No. 6 Indiana. Freshman QB Tommy Carr started in place of Bryce Underwood and it was clear that Carr is not immediately going to usurp the former five-star recruit.

Michigan needed a last-second field goal simply to get the game to overtime before Indiana QB Josh Hoover rushed for a score to open overtime.

From there, a touchdown was a mountain too tall for the Wolverines' offense. Michigan ran 74 plays and gained just 224 yards. That's fractionally over 3 yards a play.

If the Wolverines had a functional offense, they could be a national title contender. They don't, so they're instead reduced to playing spoiler in the Big Ten after dropping to 1-3 in conference play. Upcoming games against Rutgers and Michigan State could be a nice salve, but the season ends in a suddenly meaningless game at Oregon before No. 9 UCLA and No. 3 Ohio State.

Like Oregon, Michigan should get bowl eligible. But all three of the Aggies, Ducks and Wolverines are going to be much closer to 6-6 and a bottom-tier bowl bid than sniffing the College Football Playoff.

Here are the rest of this week's winners and losers.

Wyoming QB Tyler Hughes: Hughes threw for two scores and rushed for another while producing one of the best runs you'll see all season. And it somehow didn't end up as a touchdown. Just look at how Hughes stayed upright.

The Cowboys beat Air Force 28-14 on Friday night to move to 4-1 in the Mountain West and 5-3 overall. With a late-season game remaining against New Mexico, Wyoming is very much in the mix for the Mountain West title.

Virginia Tech: The Hokies got bowl eligible by moving to 6-2 with a 20-16 win at Clemson on Saturday night. What's the big deal? Well, Virginia Tech was 3-9 in 2025. The Hokies could flip that record in James Franklin's first season.

Virginia Tech outscored Clemson 10-0 in the fourth quarter as Ethan Grunkemeyer hit Luke Reynolds for the game-winning score with 1:44 to go. Clemson is now 4-3 overall and 2-2 in the ACC after freshman QB Tait Reynolds was 20-of-26 and threw for just 153 yards.

Florida Atlantic WR Easton Messer: The Owls' 51-49 win over Rice was a game full of big plays. And Messer had his fair share. The 100-point contest featured nine touchdowns that were 30 yards or longer. Messer had 12 catches for 162 yards and two touchdowns, rushed three times for 18 yards and two scores and also had an 82-yard punt return. The two teams combined for over 1,000 yards as Rice rushed 51 times for 499 yards.

Kansas: The Jayhawks were not going to let their losing streak to Baylor hit 20 years. Kansas QB Isaiah Marshall scored on a 15-yard run with 1:13 left to give KU a 25-24 win over the Bears after blocking Baylor's go-ahead field goal attempt.

It was Kansas' first win over Baylor since 2007. Before Saturday, Baylor had won 14 straight games over the Jayhawks. It's also a victory that's a massive boost to Kansas' hopes of making a bowl game. The win pushed KU to 3-4 overall with games remaining against BYU and at Oklahoma State.

No. 16 USC: The Trojans lost another Big Ten road game they were supposed to win. USC fell to 4-7 on the road in the Big Ten with a loss at Wisconsin. USC is now 15-14 overall on the road or at neutral sites under Lincoln Riley as USC is still a second-class team in the Big Ten. If there was ever a year for the Trojans to be in contention for the Big Ten title, 2026 is it. Instead, USC scored seven points. A Riley team had never scored only seven points in a game until Saturday night.

Deion Sanders: Colorado led Oklahoma State 24-23 at halftime. It was a great opportunity for the Buffaloes to get a road conference win with a strong second half.

Well, uh, Colorado's second half was the opposite of strong. Oklahoma State outscored the Buffaloes 34-0 over the final two quarters for a 57-24 victory. QB Drew Mestemaker finished 21-of-36 for 386 yards and four touchdowns as OSU had 598 yards of total offense.

Colorado fumbled on the first offensive play of the second half and then punted four more times and Isaac Wilson had two interceptions after halftime. The Buffaloes gained 46 yards on their final drive before time expired. Before that, Colorado had gained 45 yards the entire half. Sanders' team is now 0-4 and in the basement of the Big 12.

James Madison: The Dukes made the College Football Playoff last season by going undefeated in the regular season. They were probably going to have to do the same thing again in 2026 for another playoff appearance.

The undefeated season slipped away Thursday night. JMU lost 34-31 at Appalachian State in overtime after a touchdown with just a few seconds left was needed to get the game to OT in the first place. It was the first regular-season loss for James Madison in over a year and it's now a virtual certainty that the Group of Six representative in the College Football Playoff will come from the Pac-12 or the American Conference.

Virginia: The Cavaliers have now lost three of their last four games after a 19-16 Friday night loss at home to Duke. The Blue Devils' game-winning score came on a 28-yard TD pass from star RB Nate Sheppard. Yes, really.

After making the ACC title game a season ago, the Cavaliers are 4-4 overall and 2-3 in ACC play. A second straight trip to Charlotte isn't happening.

TCU: The Horned Frogs are quickly staring at the prospect of a losing season. TCU lost 24-20 at home to West Virginia despite QB Jaden Craig throwing for 372 yards. As has been the norm this season, turnovers doomed TCU. The Horned Frogs committed three turnovers — Craig threw an interception and fumbled twice — while WVU QB Michael Hawkins continued his impressive 2026 with three more touchdowns.

TCU is now 3-4 overall and 1-3 in the Big 12. They also have three of their five remaining games against ranked opponents.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal, este Clásico no se lo pierde
articles.standfirst: Fue baja en el alirón de mayo: es su primer cruce contra el Real Madrid en el Spotify Camp Nou
articles.summary: Fue baja en el alirón de mayo: es su primer cruce contra el Real Madrid en el Spotify Camp Nou
articles.body: Esta noche, como casi siempre, todas las miradas estarán puestas sobre Lamine Yamal. El extremo culé disputará su primer Clásico en el Spotify Camp Nou. No es, no obstante, el primer cruce del joven internacional contra el Real Madrid, pese a tener sólo 19 años será el ¡décimo! Se perdió, por lesión, el último del curso pasado, el del alirón azulgrana ante su grada, pero esta jornada estará sobre el césped. Es uno de los grandes argumentos ofensivos del Barça y uno de sus profesionales más en forma. Lamine vivirá esta noche un encuentro especial. Será su primer Clásico en el Spotify Camp Nou: se perdió el cruce del 10 de mayo pasado, en el que el Barça festejó la consecución de LaLiga, como consecuencia de una lesión en el bíceps femoral de la pierna izquierda. Faltó en aquel histórico partido contra el eterno rival, pero el joven atacante, de 19 años, es casi todo un experto ya en cruces contra el Real Madrid. El canterano culé ha intervenido en nueve partidos contra los del Santiago Bernabéu: 5 en LaLiga, tres en la Supercopa de España y uno en la Copa del Rey. Cuatro fueron finales, y se proclamó vencedor en tres. En estos compromisos, logró un balance de 5 victorias y cuatro derrotas, y marcó tres goles y repartió dos asistencias. Hoy jugará, por lo tanto, el décimo Clásico, y lo hará en un gran momento de forma. Lamine suma ocho goles y seis asistencias en LaLiga: ocupa la tercera posición en la clasificación de máximos realizadores del torneo nacional regular, sólo le superan su amigo y compañero Raphinha (12) y Mbappé (9). Sus registros son históricos: únicamente dos jugadores españoles lograron más tantos que el profesional de Rocafonda tras los nueve primeros partidos en una campaña desde principios del siglo: David Villa en la temporada 2008-09 y Diego Costa en la 2013-14. Ambos firmaron diez dianas. Pero, además, el extremo derecho es el único futbolista que ha marcado cinco o más goles (8) y repartido cinco o más asistencias (6) esta temporada. Lamine llega al Clásico de hoy en un excelente momento de forma, tanto anímico como deportivo. Es una de las grandes armas de Flick para seguir con la gran racha culé: el Barça, líder de la tabla, ha ganado los nueve primeros partidos de LaLiga. Con autoridad.

articles.title: Deion Sanders, Colorado vs. OK State Final Box Score, Top Player Stats and Highlights
articles.summary: Deion Sanders and the Colorado Buffaloes fell 57-24 to the Oklahoma State Cowboys after an explosive second half led by Drew Mestemaker and the Cowboys' offense.
articles.body:
Deion Sanders and the Colorado Buffaloes fell 57-24 to the Oklahoma State Cowboys after an explosive second half led by Drew Mestemaker and the Cowboys' offense.

The Buffaloes entered their road matchup as staggering 13.5-point underdogs, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

After leading 24-23 at halftime, Colorado appeared poised for an upset. However, offensive turnovers and a defensive collapse allowed Oklahoma State to outscore the Buffaloes 34-0 in the second half and secure the win.

Colorado remains winless in Big 12 play at 0-4, dropping to 2-5 overall. Oklahoma State improved to 5-2 overall and 3-1 in conference play, adding to a season that includes a marquee win over the No. 6 Oregon Ducks and a narrow 35-32 loss to the No. 20 Houston Cougars last week.

After finishing 3-9 last season, the Buffaloes appear to be on a similar trajectory this year. Colorado's last winning season came in 2024, when the Buffaloes finished 9-4 behind an offense led by Shedeur Sanders and Travis Hunter.

The 2-4 Buffaloes gave 4-2 Oklahoma State a run for its money through the opening two quarters, entering halftime with a one-point lead, 24-23.

Despite Mestemaker and the Cowboys' opening the game with a score in under a minute, Buffalo responded by scoring on each of its first two possessions in the first quarter.

Wilson found running back JaQuail Smith for a short touchdown pass and DeAndre Moore Jr. on a 15-yard shotgun pass to give the Buffaloes a 14-7 lead after the first quarter.

Oklahoma State scored on every possession in the second quarter, notching three field goals and a 14-yard touchdown pass from Mestemaker to Justin Bowick.

However, the Cowboys' defense struggled to contain Wilson, who added a rushing touchdown and helped put the Buffaloes in field goal range to take a one-point lead into halftime.

Oklahoma State erupted out of halftime, outscoring Colorado 14-0 to take a 37-24 lead behind a touchdown pass from Mestemaker and a rushing score from William Mason. The Cowboys' defense also stepped up, intercepting Wilson at Oklahoma State's 30-yard line and forcing a fumble from the Colorado quarterback that was returned to Colorado's own 13-yard line.

Colorado's struggles continued in the fourth quarter, as the Buffaloes surrendered two field goals, another touchdown pass from Mestemaker and a rushing score. Wilson added to his costly evening with his third turnover of the game, throwing another interception as Oklahoma State pulled away for the win.

Colorado will host the Kentucky State Wildcats next Saturday at 2 p.m. ET, while Oklahoma State will hit the road to face the Iowa State Cyclones at 7 p.m. ET that same day.

articles.title: El Clasico preview: Barcelona’s goal machine meets its biggest test yet
articles.summary: It’s still not Nov but there’s already a sense of inevitability around the La Liga season.
articles.body: It’s still not Nov but there’s already a sense of inevitability around the La Liga season. Barcelona have been a free-scoring beast, winning all their nine games in emphatic fashion and are already six points clear of Real Madrid, who are still getting used to Jose Mourinho’s ways.A victory at Camp Nou on Sunday in the season’s first Clasico will hand Barcelona a runaway lead. Given the way the season has progressed so far, it could well be game, set and match.English winger Anthony Gordon, in his first season for the Catalan giants, has been one of the important cogs in the wheel. Though he has scored only once in the Liga so far, the mild-mannered attacker has been a livewire down the left.When TOI asked him ahead about the secret sauce behind Barca’s indomitable goal-scoring spree this season, the winger said, “It’s a mix of the ability of some incredible players and having a relentless mindset to keep going. When we’ve been three, four goals up, we haven’t stopped attacking and our need and want for goals never went down. That reflects in the number of goals we’ve scored,” Gordon, who has fitted in well to coach Hansi Flick’s high-press attacking system, said.The 25-year-old was part of a Newcastle United team that put up a good fight in the first leg of the Champions League round-of-16 last season before being routed 2-7 at Camp Nou. But the Spanish champions are looking deadlier this season and Gordon attributes that to “players coming into their own”.“They’re showing a lot of character and personality. Lamine (Yamal) has gone to a different level, even Pau Cubarsí. The likes of Marc Bernal and Javi Espart are also really taking a step into the team. We have a very young team and for someone like Rodri to come and really calm the team down with his football intelligence has been very important,” Gordon said.(Watch El Clasico exclusively on FanCode at 1.30 am)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
