articles.title: Bill Belichick, UNC vs. Syracuse Final Box Score, Top Player Stats and Highlights
articles.summary: Bill Belichick and the North Carolina Tar Heels suffered a stunning overtime upset, falling 31-30 at home to the Syracuse Orange after Syracuse converted a game-winning two-point attempt to seal the road victory.
articles.body:
Bill Belichick and the North Carolina Tar Heels suffered a stunning overtime upset, falling 31-30 at home to the Syracuse Orange after Syracuse converted a game-winning two-point attempt to seal the road victory.

North Carolina was an 8.5-point favorite entering its matchup against Syracuse on Saturday, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

Watch: Birds eye view of field rush after CFB upset

The Tar Heels fell to 4-3 overall and 2-2 in conference play, snapping a two-game winning streak that included a statement rivalry victory over Duke and an upset win over the No. 25 Pittsburgh Panthers.

Meanwhile, Syracuse secured its first conference win of the season, improving to 3-4 overall and 1-4 in conference play with the overtime victory in Chapel Hill.

North Carolina held Syracuse scoreless in the opening quarter, controlling the clock while adding a field goal and a shotgun touchdown pass from Edwards Jr. to Jordan Shipp to take a 10-0 lead.

Syracuse got on the board early in the second quarter after a 7:15 drive, adding a field goal.

Meanwhile, North Carolina added a 39-yard field goal to take a 13-3 lead into halftime.

Coming out of halftime, the Tar Heels forced Syracuse to punt before Edwards Jr. led a drive downfield that ended with Demon June rushing for a 25-yard touchdown, his seventh score of the season. UNC led 20-10 into the final quarter.

Syracuse found its first score of the second half in the fourth, scoring on a one-play, 76-yard touchdown pass.

North Carolina answered with a field goal to maintain a six-point lead, but the Orange found their rhythm, scoring on back-to-back possessions to tie the game after a missed extra point and forcing overtime.

In overtime, North Carolina struck first with a touchdown pass from Edwards Jr. to June, putting the pressure on Syracuse to respond. The Orange answered, as Steve Angeli found a receiver in the end zone before a successful two-point conversion sealed the road win.

North Carolina will host coach Mario Cristobal and the No. 1 Miami Hurricanes next Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: El Clasico awaits a Yamal vs Mbappe showdown on Mourinho’s return to La Liga
articles.summary: Barcelona vs Real Madrid will mark the return of Spanish football’s fiercest rivalry between two star-studded teams.
articles.body:
Barcelona, Spain – It has been 15 years since Jose Mourinho was first thrown into the ring of fire at Camp Nou and the famously polarising manager’s Real Madrid side was handed a La Liga battering by Barcelona.

The home team’s supporters have not forgotten that cold November night from 2010, when Pep Guardiola’s men stamped their authority with a 5-0 win.

It became an enduring image of a rivalry that spilled from the pitch onto the touchline, sparking heated confrontations among players and bitter exchanges between managers for years to come.

Now, Barcelona – the city and the club – are ready to “welcome back” Mourinho on his second stint as the manager of their fiercest rival .

“I remember the 5-0 [scoreline] but also the tension,” recalls Aleix Soler, a Barcelona fan.

“You’d spend the whole week arguing about the game even before a ball was kicked,” he tells Al Jazeera at a Barcelona fan zone.

The 35-year-old culer – as Barcelona’s supporters are known – will watch the match, having also attended games during Mourinho’s first Madrid spell.

“Beating Madrid is always special, but against Mourinho, you’re still smiling on Monday morning.”

As Mourinho returns to the fixture after 13 years on Sunday, he will face another Barcelona side that has set a punishing pace in the league.

The spotlight will be on Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe – with their growing rivalry adding another dramatic layer to the plot.

The two forwards meet a day before the Ballon d’Or award ceremony in London, bringing individual ambition to a contest that isn’t shorn of consequences for either club.

Barcelona have won all nine of their league games, scoring 39 goals, and lead Madrid by six points.

Victory would stretch that gap to nine. A Madrid win would not only reduce it to three points, but also inject new belief in Mourinho’s side.

Mourinho acknowledged the significance of the occasion after his team’s Champions League victory over RB Leipzig on Wednesday.

“It’s another league match, but it’s not a match like the others,” he told local broadcaster Movistar.

Madrid are third in La Liga standings, behind Atletico Madrid, and have lost six of their past seven Clasicos. Mourinho must find a way to interrupt that pattern before the title chase intensifies.

While Hansi Flick has made this fixture a source of strength for Barcelona in his two years as manager, the hosts approach it with their own questions after a 4-2 defeat at Paris Saint-Germain , their first loss of the season, on Tuesday.

Barcelona scored freely against Getafe, Galatasaray and Real Betis before travelling to France. In Paris, their attacking threat remained but defensive absences and the spaces opened up to PSG made the evening uncomfortable.

Barcelona defenders Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde were out injured, leaving Flick with Xavi Espart and Joao Cancelo as full-back options on either side of Pau Cubarsi and Gerard Martin.

Kounde remained absent from training on Friday, while midfielder Dani Olmo’s adductor injury further narrowed the coach’s options.

Madrid enjoyed a more encouraging European evening, beating Leipzig 4-1 with goals from Bernardo Silva, Arda Guler, Mbappe and Yan Diomande.

Their three wins from three Champions League games offer a foundation, even if domestic consistency has proved harder to establish.

However, they will face Barcelona without the suspended Vinicius Junior, removing one of their most dangerous runners and leaving Mourinho with another decision to make about Mbappe.

Yan Diomande offers an alternative on the left, while Guler’s passing and Jude Bellingham’s movement could be essential to getting Madrid’s leading scorer into dangerous positions.

The task begins with escaping Barcelona’s pressure. If Madrid can move the ball beyond the first challenge and find a passer facing forward, Mbappe can attack the space behind Flick’s defensive line.

For Barcelona, maintaining pressure on that passer will be as important as tracking the run. Retreat too readily, and they risk losing the compact shape that allows them to recover possession and keep attacks coming.

Federico Valverde’s recent deployment at right-back gives Madrid another route forward, with his overlapping runs complementing teammates who move inside.

Whether Mourinho keeps him there will help determine the balance between creativity and defensive cover in midfield.

Madrid must decide how much attention they can afford to give Yamal .

The young sensation’s dribbling can draw a second defender towards Barcelona’s right wing, but that help comes at a cost elsewhere as Pedri can redirect possession towards the space left open.

Meanwhile, Raphinha’s movement threatens opponents concentrating on the ball, and his 12 league goals underline the danger of treating Barcelona as a one-man attack.

Stopping Yamal from beating his marker will achieve little success if the supporting defensive movements leave another player free.

For Real Madrid fans, one glorious night at Camp Nou could be seen as a turning point.

“Winning there would make me believe we can win the league, especially if we play with courage”, says Lucia Martin, a Madrid supporter.

The 26-year-old is travelling to Barcelona with her father to attend the game, and much of her hope rests on Mbappe, although she wants the team to share the responsibility.

“When he gets the ball, I always think something can happen, but we can’t spend 90 minutes waiting for him to rescue us.”

Despite leading all conversations around the match, Yamal and Mbappe will rarely confront each other directly; their influence will be measured in the problems they create for everyone else.

Yamal has eight goals and six assists in nine league appearances. Mbappe has nine goals and two assists across the same number of games.

One can pull defenders towards the ball before releasing a teammate, the other can force them backwards with the threat of a run.

Both are nominees for the upcoming Ballon d’Or and although the match falls outside the assessment period for this year’s award, it will serve as the perfect build-up to one of the most hotly-contested awards in recent years.

Before football celebrates its outstanding performers in London, two of its strongest claimants to the title of world’s best will share a stage where reputations are tested under exceptional pressure and strengthen their claim as the world’s best.

On the eve of the Ballon d’Or, Yamal has a chance to extend Barcelona’s perfect start and deepen Madrid’s frustration.

For Mbappe, there is the opportunity to bring his team back into the race at their rival’s expense.

articles.title: Arch Manning, Trinidad Chambliss' Final Box Score Stats, Highlights, Draft Stock from Texas-Ole Miss
articles.summary: Arch Manning and the Texas Longhorns escaped with a 34-27 win over Trinidad Chambliss and the Ole Miss Rebels on Saturday, holding off a furious second-half comeback attempt by the Rebels to secure the victory in Austin.
articles.body:
Arch Manning and the Texas Longhorns escaped with a 34-27 win over Trinidad Chambliss and the Ole Miss Rebels on Saturday, holding off a furious second-half comeback attempt by the Rebels to secure the victory in Austin.

Despite entering the matchup on a two-game losing streak, Manning and the Longhorns were 3.5-point favorites over the Rebels, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

Texas held Ole Miss to just three points in the first half before being outscored 24-10 after the break, setting the stage for an instant classic between the No. 7 Rebels and No. 19 Longhorns.

It was all Longhorns to open Saturday's game.

Manning completed 13-of-19 passes for 171 yards, one touchdown and one interception to lead Texas to a 24-3 halftime lead.

Meanwhile, the Longhorns defense held Chambliss to 63 yards on 6-of-18 passing, with no touchdowns and two interceptions. It marked Chambliss' first multi-interception game as a Rebel.

Manning rushed for a touchdown in the first quarter to give Texas a 10-3 lead before the Longhorns scored twice more in the second. Manning connected with Ryan Wingo on a deep, 50-yard touchdown pass, and Michael Terry III rushed for a score before halftime.

Manning fumbled coming out of halftime, and Ole Miss defensive end Kam Franklin returned it for a touchdown. The Rebels added another score when Chambliss connected with Horatio Fields, cutting the deficit to 24-17.

On Ole Miss' first drive of the fourth quarter, Chambliss found Fields again for a 27-yard touchdown pass to tie the game at 24-24, capping a 21-0 run against Texas.

Manning threw his second interception of the game, but Ole Miss failed to capitalize on the turnover. Manning bounced back with his second rushing touchdown of the game to put Texas back in front.

A blocked 58-yard field goal attempt by Ole Miss and a field goal from Texas extended the Longhorns' lead to 10 points late in the game.

Ole Miss added a field goal with 1:22 remaining in the fourth quarter and successfully recovered an onside kick to get the ball back and make a potentially game-winning drive.

Despite a late push from Chambliss, who delivered several impressive throws and found open receivers downfield, time eventually ran out on Ole Miss. Texas held on to secure the win in Austin, escaping after the Rebels' second-half surge threatened to complete the comeback.

ESPN's Jordan Reid noted Oct. 9 that Chambliss has risen to a potential top-three quarterback pick in the first round after leading his team to one of three one-loss seasons in the SEC.

That would put Chambliss behind only Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker and Miami's Darian Mensah while placing him ahead of his Saturday rival, Manning (No. 5), as well as Notre Dame's CJ Carr and Oregon's Dante Moore.

"I've seen him play live multiple times now, and you just hold your breath every single time because he throws strike after strike," an NFC assistant general manager said, according to Reid. "He's smaller and won't be for everyone that has a need there, but he's one that makes you think really hard about making an exception to your normal rules in the draft room."

Chambliss' age, a second-year senior, and tendency to make reckless decisions in an attempt to make a highlight rather than take the easy option to secure a win, have drawn criticism this season.

Ole Miss' lone loss this season came against Florida in a lopsided 52-28 defeat in late September. The Rebels have also earned big wins over Missouri, LSU and Louisville.

Chambliss has yet to throw for fewer than 210 yards in a game, notching 14 touchdowns and 1,676 passing yards with just four interceptions heading into his matchup against Texas.

Meanwhile, Manning ranks as the No. 5 quarterback prospect, potentially pushing him into the early part of Day 2 of the draft, according to Reid.

As the nephew of former NFL stars Peyton and Eli Manning, Arch has faced constant pressure and criticism this season while leading Texas to a 4-2 record. Heading into Saturday's matchup, he had thrown for 1,295 yards and 11 touchdowns, with five interceptions.

"He'll always be graded on a different scale because of the name, but I think someone will fall in love with what he can be in a few years," an AFC scout said, according to Reid. "I don't think he's the best in the class, but his flashes in games are fascinating and a preview of what could happen down the road."

Manning's resume has been less impressive than Chambliss' this season, averaging 215 passing yards per game while recording three games with fewer than 200 yards.

In recent weeks, the senior's ceiling has come into question following back-to-back losses to unranked Oklahoma and Florida. However, he has also earned signature wins over No. 1 Ohio State and No. 14 Tennessee.

Both quarterbacks struggled at different points in the game, with Chambliss faltering in the first half and Manning facing trouble after the break. Chambliss threw a career-high three interceptions as a Rebel, while Manning committed three turnovers of his own, throwing two interceptions and losing a fumble.

Despite their struggles, Manning came out on top against the higher-ranked Ole Miss squad, showing poise in the closing minutes after the Rebels' 21-0 run. He led Texas on two scoring drives down the stretch to help secure the win.

Neither quarterback delivered a standout performance, and Manning's win is unlikely to shift the draft conversation in his favor over Chambliss, despite Texas coming out on top.

Ole Miss will host the Auburn Tigers at 12:45 p.m. ET next Saturday, while Texas will host the Mississippi State Bulldogs at 7:30 p.m. ET that same day.

articles.title: USC falls apart in Madison, losing to unranked Wisconsin
articles.summary: The Trojans suffered a crushing road loss as almost nothing went right all evening.
articles.body:
Lincoln Riley and his USC Trojans headed into the bye week with serious optimism after knocking off Penn State in front of over 114,000 Nittany Lion fans wearing white. On Saturday evening, however, a complete 180. The Trojans fell flat on their faces at Camp Randall Stadium, losing 24-7 to the Wisconsin Badgers.

Chances of an appearance in the College Football Playoff are now close to none, with USC almost certainly needing to run the table through its final four games. Unfortunately for them, three of those matchups will come against Ohio State, Indiana and UCLA.

"Just flat-out didn't play good enough on any of the three sides of the ball," Riley said after the loss. "Didn't coach good enough, made critical errors on the road...I take responsibility for it. It's hard to win on the road, and you have to play a lot better than we did tonight."

It started with an offensive unit that had perhaps its worst display since Riley took over as head coach of the program. Their lowest point total since his arrival had been 17 before coming 10 short of that mark on Saturday. The Trojans had also not been held under 14 points in a game since 2018.

Jayden Maiava threw the ball a season-high 50 times, completing 31 passes for a single touchdown and two interceptions. Both of his giveaways came in a nightmare first quarter for USC that smothered any sort of opportunity to get off to a fast start on the road.

"Flat out, I just didn't play great," Maiava said. "I got to play better for my teammates."

When things weren't going right through the air, they were somehow going worse on the ground. The Trojans managed to carry the ball 25 times for a total of -17 rush yards. Maiava finished with -57 himself.

Through all the dismay, USC only found itself trailing 10-7 at halftime thanks to a four-yard touchdown grab from tight end Taniela Tupou in the second quarter. The full unraveling took place in the final 30 minutes of the contest.

The Badgers only continued to expand upon their three-point advantage, which had initially been provided via a five-yard rushing touchdown late in the second quarter from former Trojan Bryan Jackson.

Wisconsin quarterback Colton Joseph handed the ball off on six of 10 plays on the Badgers' opening drive of the half, capping it off with a 16-yard touchdown pass to Chris Brooks Jr. for the score. USC finished its next drive by seeing Caden Chittenden's 44-yard field goal attempt get blocked.

Joseph led yet another scoring drive in the fourth quarter that chewed nearly eight minutes of clock, with Ryan Schwendeman's one-yard rushing touchdown helping the Badgers extend their lead to 24-7 with just 5:21 to go. On the drive beforehand, it was more disaster from the special teams unit for the Trojans, as Chittenden missed a 58-yard attempt that came up way short. His season-high for a made field goal had been just 39 yards.

By the time the clock had ticked its way to the end of the fourth quarter, USC had taken the form of a team that was discouraged and defeated. They dropped to 6-2 on the season and 3-2 in the Big Ten. Wisconsin, meanwhile, earned its second victory against a ranked opponent and improved to 5-2.

A tale of total opposites left the Trojans on the embarrassing end of a defeat that will once again have the fanbase calling for Riley's job. This time around, are the complaints genuinely justified? They very well might be.

Wisconsin was simply relentless in the run game, putting the ball on the ground 42 times and accumulating 142 rushing yards. Joseph needed to throw the ball just 14 times and had only 58 passing yards.

Maiava was sacked five times. USC was flagged for six penalties that totaled 51 yards, while Wisconsin committed just four for 30 yards. As Riley said, those are critical errors. You can't expect to win in front of 71,750 at Camp Randall if that's the product.

The noise from critics will be at a new high for the 2026 season, but the Trojans need to pick themselves up off the mat quickly with No. 3 Ohio State coming to the Coliseum on Halloween night. Another performance like Saturday's against the Badgers, and things will get even scarier in Los Angeles.

One possible beam of light for the Trojans: the Buckeyes will be without starting quarterback Julian Sayin, who is out indefinitely after injuring his shoulder on Oct. 17 at Indiana. Unfortunately, Jeremiah Smith still exists, and the Heisman frontrunner will be hungry to add another marquee performance to his ledger.

articles.title: Austin FC rallies to beat Sporting KC, keep slim MLS playoff hopes alive
articles.summary: Myrto Uzuni scored twice as Austin FC rallied for a 2-1 MLS win over Sporting Kansas City at Sporting Park in Kansas City, Kansas.
articles.body:
One down, three to go - and some help - for Austin FC .

The Verde and Black's MLS playoff hopes hinge on a four-game winning streak and a lot of friendly results elsewhere around the league to end the year, but Austin FC took the first step in that unlikely process Saturday.

Myrto Uzuni scored twice in the final 30 minutes as the Verde and Black rallied for a 2-1 win over Sporting Kansas City at Sporting Park in Kansas City, Kansas.

Uzuni now has 13 goals across all competitions, including nine in MLS play, which leads the club.

It was a mostly good showing for Austin FC, though it was a bit lucky in the final 15 minutes when Kansas City failed to finish some chances, most notably Stephen Afrifa sending a shot inside the Verde and Black's six-yard box wide of the goal. Austin FC had 56% of possession and finished with an expected goals stat of 1.77, according to the Apple TV broadcast.

The club also won with backup goalie Damian Las playing.

Afrifa put Kansas City ahead early in the second half with a well-taken shot in the box.

Austin FC (8-13-10, 34 points, 14th West) plays Wednesday at home against Real Salt Lake.

articles.title: Neymar, expulsado por la 'Ley Vinicius'
articles.standfirst: El delantero del Santos vio la roja por taparse la boca mientras se dirigía a un rival
articles.summary: El delantero del Santos vio la roja por taparse la boca mientras se dirigía a un rival
articles.body: Neymar, delantero del Santos, fue expulsado este sábado por taparse la boca mientras, aparentemente, discutía con un jugador del Bahía en un partido correspondiente a la trigésima segunda jornada del Campeonato Brasileño. El número 10 estaba hablando con Rodrigo Nestor en el círculo central antes del inicio de la segunda mitad, cuando en un momento determinado se lleva la mano a la boca y le dice algo al centrocampista del equipo de Salvador. En ese instante, Nestor se va directo hacia el árbitro para denunciar el comportamiento del exjugador del Barcelona y del París Saint-Germain (PSG). Antes incluso de reiniciarse el juego, el árbitro es llamado por el VAR, que le muestra la imagen de 'Ney' tapándose la boca. En consecuencia, decide expulsarlo con roja directa, al encuadrar el gesto del atacante en la bautizada como 'Ley Vinícius Júnior', que se aplica en el 'Brasileirão'. Nestor y Neymar ya habían discutido en la primera mitad. En declaraciones a SporTV durante el descanso, el volante del Bahía criticó duramente a Neymar. Relató que le fue a dar la mano y que el exjugador de la selección brasileña respondió lanzándole la pelota al cuerpo. "Después escuché una serie de cosas. Mis padres me educaron muy bien, se lo agradezco mucho y sé perfectamente de dónde vengo. Nací en Itaquera; era difícil llegar adonde he llegado y estoy orgulloso de vestir la camiseta del Bahía. Él sabe lo que me dijo. Fue una falta de respeto hacia mí y hacia la camiseta del Bahía", explicó. Y completó sobre la estrella del Santos: "Es un ídolo para todo el mundo como jugador, pero hoy falló como persona por la forma en que habló. No se deben hacer ese tipo de cosas. Mis padres me educaron muy bien y les agradezco la educación que me dieron. Yo nunca diría algo así". Repreguntado sobre qué le dijo exactamente, Nestor se negó a reproducir las palabras del dorsal 10 "porque hay niños viendo y no estuvo bien". Tras esas declaraciones, Neymar habló con Nestor instantes antes de la segunda mitad, se tapó la boca por un momento y terminó expulsado. El exdelantero del Al-Hilal saudí luego reconoció que se equivocó, pero que Nestor exageró porque se fue en dirección al árbitro antes de que le dijera nada. Para entonces, el Bahía ganaba 1-0 gracias al gol de Luciano Juba, pero el Santos, con un hombre menos, insistió y logró un punto por medio de Luan Peres en el minuto 93. El encuentro estuvo marcado por un fuerte temporal de lluvias que dejó el césped de Vila Belmiro lleno de charcos y en una situación prácticamente inviable para jugar al fútbol. Pese a todo, el partido se disputó hasta el final.

images.caption: Imagen del VAR con Neymar tapándose la boca.

articles.title: Lincoln Riley's Updated Contract Buyout After Jayden Maiava, USC's Upset Loss vs. Wisconsin
articles.summary: Two sources (247Sports' Matt Zenitz and ESPN's Paul Finebaum) reported earlier this fall that the buyout on USC football head coach Lincoln Riley's 10-year, $110 million contract is worth $70 million.
articles.body:
Two sources (247Sports' Matt Zenitz and ESPN's Paul Finebaum ) reported earlier this fall that the buyout on USC football head coach Lincoln Riley's 10-year, $110 million contract is worth $70 million.

That figure comes to mind in the wake of No. 16 USC football's 24-7 road loss to unranked Wisconsin on Saturday.

USC started the year as a potential College Football Playoff candidate, but the road to get there is treacherous now.

Unranked Teams Cause Chaos in Rankings 📊

A home date with No. 3 Ohio State looms before the Trojans visit No. 6 Indiana. USC should be a big favorite over 2-5 (0-4 Big Ten) Maryland, but the annual matchup with crosstown rival UCLA ends the regular season.

The Bruins are undefeated at 7-0 and ranked ninth in the AP poll but will rise a few spots after a few upsets ahead of them.

If the chalk holds, 6-2 USC is finishing the year at 7-5 in head coach Lincoln Riley's fifth season at the helm. Riley arrived in town in 2022 with great fanfare after great success at Oklahoma, and his first season went well (11-3, Cotton Bowl appearance, 12th in the final AP poll).

His last three-plus seasons have not for the most part. USC went 15-11 over the 2023 and 2024 seasons and did not make the final AP poll.

The Trojans were better in 2025 (9-4) and finished 20th in the poll, but now this year's team might be regressing. Of note, they nearly lost to a 2-6 Rutgers team before prevailing 42-35. No. 20 Oregon also beat USC 41-27 in Los Angeles.

USC does have five other wins, but those teams rank as follows in the Sagarin ratings : 122nd (San Jose State), 82nd (Fresno State), 83rd (Louisiana), 41st (Washington) and 36th (Penn State).

The Wisconsin game is simply a bad loss. USC had minus-17 rushing yards while allowing the Badgers to scamper for 142 yards and two scores on the ground. Wisconsin also won while accounting for just 58 passing yards.

Ultimately, the program seems to be going in the wrong direction, even with a talented and capable quarterback at the helm in Jayden Maiava, whose 3,711 passing yards led the Big Ten in 2025.

USC doesn't have much time to bounce back, as OSU now rolls into town on Saturday evening at 7:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: What LSU Tigers coach Lane Kiffin called ‘abnormal’ after win over Auburn Tigers
articles.summary: LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin addressed one of the biggest factors in the program’s 2026 CFB season after a 38-17 win over the Auburn Tigers. The Tigers...
articles.body:
LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin addressed one of the biggest factors in the program's 2026 CFB season after a 38-17 win over the Auburn Tigers.

The Tigers fell behind the competitive pack early in the 2026 CFB season with losses to Ole Miss and Kentucky in the first five weeks, which has dented their hopes of reaching the College Football Playoffs.

After LSU picked up a 38-17 win over Auburn on October 24, Coach Kiffin made it a point to remind everyone about the real circumstances that have defined LSU's start to the season.

Lane Kiffin thinks LSU Tigers' 2026 season has been abnormal

Kiffin spoke to the media after the win over Auburn and was asked about the best games that LSU have played this season, ending it with an admission that LSU's injury situation and their results are abnormal.

"We've played really good games this year. The opening game, it was about as well as you could have played… Last week, they didn't score against us. We've played really well. We've had five games where our backups are in at the end of the game, including 3 SEC games. That's very abnormal."

These comments come a week after Kiffin explosively told Mississippi State to stop complaining about losing key players to injury, because LSU and other top teams have also lost players to injury already.

The Tigers have lost LB Whit Weeks, Safety Dashawn Spears, WR Phillip Wright III, and are expected to be without key contributors like Charles Ross II and DT Richard Anderson.

Thankfully, LSU did see TE Trey'Dez Green return to the field against Auburn, while WR Jackson Harris avoided major injury. DE Princewill Umanmielen is expected to return soon as well.

QB Sam Leavitt is playing through a hamstring injury as well, so Kiffin is fair to hold the opinion he does about the team's injury crisis being abnormal, especially with their recent results.

If the Tigers manage to go the rest of the season without a loss, they will presumably be locked into the CFP. Even one more loss makes their qualifying situation dicey, so LSU and Kiffin will hope they can push through their injury crisis and continue extracting results on the field.

articles.title: Arsenal Women finally managed a win. But will it be enough for Renee Slegers?
articles.summary: Actions speak louder than words — and no more words were needed. At the final whistle, Renee Slegers squatted down before springing back up and fist-pumping....
articles.body:
Actions speak louder than words — and no more words were needed.

At the final whistle, Renee Slegers squatted down before springing back up and fist-pumping. The Arsenal head coach turned to her staff and hugged them.

It was a moment of relief, a big exhale, the pressure valve on the Dutchwoman had been slightly released. Finally, after seven weeks, Arsenal registered a league win, only their second of the domestic campaign, coming from behind in the north London derby to beat Tottenham Hotspur 2-1.

The magnitude of the result was reflected in the players' reactions.

Instead of forming their customary team huddle at full time, the Arsenal squad lined up, hand in hand and held them aloft to the 4,000-strong travelling fans, their largest travelling support in the WSL in two and a half years.

Arsenal, so used to celebrating wins, wanted to mark the moment even though some may argue their celebrations were disproportionate to the occasion.

Heading into the derby, all eyes were on Arsenal, who sat eighth in the WSL, 12 points adrift of leaders Manchester City. For the first time, they had not won in five league games and had drawn the most league games since the start of last season (nine). Despite winning 10 of their 13 north London derbies, they were far from favourites.

Players returned from the international break reinvigorated, but the boost in energy was sucked out following last weekend's 1-1 draw with Birmingham. They responded with a higher level of training intensity last week, something Slegers had asked for.

The pressure on Arsenal mounted when Cathinka Tindberg's towering header put Tottenham 1-0 up inside 13 minutes. Georgia Stanway's equaliser, a thunderous first-time strike from Alessia Russo's cutback, embodied the grit Arsenal needed.

Ultimately, Russo's composure, especially given her patchy start to the season, to convert a second-half penalty was the difference. But it was a penalty that should never have been awarded.

Ella Morris was deemed to be guilty of handball after Tindberg's clearance struck her arm but new rules for the 2026-2027 season state there is no handball offence if the ball is played by a team-mate.

"The refereeing has got worse than it was last season," said Tottenham head coach Martin Ho, who wanted to speak to the officials following his post-match press conference.

Arsenal got the job done, but their problems will not vanish overnight.

They failed to take care of the ball on too many occasions even when not under pressure. Loose passes turned positions of control into fragility, landing themselves in trouble and allowing Tottenham to threaten, as was the case which led to Tindberg's goal and Victoria Pelova unleashing a shot over the bar.

They were at times still vulnerable on the counter-attack, and Slegers is still figuring out her best starting XI as she dropped left-back Ona Battle for Taylor Hinds, who had not made four matchday squads this season, introduced Caitlin Foord for her first start of the season and played Russo in her less natural position as a No 10 while starting Olivia Smith up top.

For all of their resilience against Spurs, they still failed to be ruthless against a team who have shipped 12 goals in their last two games. Despite taking the second most number of shots (135), Arsenal have the worst conversion rate (5.19 per cent), the third-worst shooting accuracy (31.1 per cent) and the fourth-lowest average xG per shot (0.1) in the WSL, according to Opta.

How they build upon this narrow victory is crucial.

Slegers will want to capitalise on the feel-good emotions. On the one hand, a busy schedule with lots of games is an opportunity to build momentum. On the other, the next block shows no signs of abating as they face Benfica in the Champions League on Wednesday followed by Aston Villa, Liverpool and then reigning European champions Barcelona.

"We have to (consolidate upon the win)," said player-of-the-match Foord, starting her first game of the season. "There's no other real solution. It's must-win games from now on. We need to leave everything out there, especially how we did today. That has to be week in week out; we need to get points on the board."

When asked about her future, Slegers has consistently said, as she did so again, post-match: "I'm not the most important in this."

"When we've gone through this, it's not about me and how I feel in this," she clarified when prompted. "It's about Arsenal and how we get Arsenal back to winning ways."

But arguably the most important person to lead players and staff through this next crucial period is the head coach. The win for Arsenal is a step in the right direction. It remains to be seen if Slegers can turn their season around.

Arsenal WFC, Women's Soccer, Women's Super League

articles.title: Arch Manning and Steve Sarkisian Silence the Noise for Now but Enormous Questions Remain for Texas
articles.summary: It was imperfect. It was stressful—far more stressful than it should have been. There were enormous mistakes intertwined with moments of absolute brilliance, especially early on. It was somehow inspiring and agonizing all at once, if such a football concoction is possible.
articles.body:
It was imperfect. It was stressful—far more stressful than it should have been. There were enormous mistakes intertwined with moments of absolute brilliance, especially early on. It was somehow inspiring and agonizing all at once, if such a football concoction is possible.

If you were merely checking the final score, Texas' 34-27 win over Ole Miss would have been satisfying enough, especially when you consider how much noise has surrounded Steve Sarkisian's program all week long.

But to leave at the score would do the game and this team a great injustice. And while we came into the game with looming questions about Texas' present and future, we left even more perplexed in many respects on a night that this program saved its season.

Early on, those questions were largely answered. Texas jumped out to an early 24-3 lead, thanks in part to quarterback Arch Manning and inspired effort from the defense, which kept quarterback Trinidad Chambliss in check.

As for Manning, his head coach floated the idea that backup KJ Lacey Jr. would play if Manning continued to struggle. His starter responded by uncorking a handful of beautiful deep balls, although one was inexcusably dropped by wideout Cam Coleman.

Along the way, Manning flashed. He showcased his speed, picking up a third and long with his legs early on. He looked sharper and more confident, at least early on. After so many questions and concerns this week, all was largely well.

The Manning saw early on largely vanished. It wasn't all his fault, of course, which has been the case all year. Manning fumbled early on, holding onto the ball far too long. Ole Miss recovered it for a touchdown, and the game flipped in a moment.

Later on, Manning unleashed a terrible interception. The Texas defense, which had been so good early, started to cave in. All the while, Sarkisian looked on in disbelief, spending much of the game yelling at officials while looking completely out of sorts.

And yes, they won. It didn't feel that way in the aftermath, but they did. Promise.

After Ole Miss recovered an onside kick that the Longhorns' special teams could have and should have recovered, Chambliss had a chance to tie the game. His Hail Mary was ultimately denied, giving the Longhorns the win it had to have.

Coming off back-to-back losses to Oklahoma and Florida, the season was on the brink. From Sarkisian to Manning, the present and future of the program felt largely up for grabs, which would sound like hyperbole for most teams given where we are on the calendar. But Texas is different.

It would be unfair to simply highlight all that went wrong on Saturday and the near unravelling. But Texas found a way, no matter how ugly those last 30 minutes were.

A loss there would have likely put this team's playoff hopes on life support. At the very least, Texas can live to fight another day. And with wins over Ohio State, Tennessee and Ole Miss—the No. 1, No. 14 and No. 7 teams at the time those games were played—the current resume is somewhat perplexing.

The same can be said about the state of the program moving forward. Saturday night didn't exactly eliminate the concerns surrounding the team's starting quarterback. It also didn't inspire a ton of confidence with the team's head coach, who wore desperation on his face all night long.

The good was very good. The bad was inexplicably bad.

In many respects, this game was a microcosm of Texas' current existence. Incredible highs mixed with incredible lows. It's a trend that ultimately prevented this team from reaching the College Football Playoff last year; it could very well be its undoing once again.

If there's one thing Texas has trademarked in the Sarkisian era, it's a lack of prolonged consistency.

With that firmly acknowledged, it was a night of celebration and relief. Forget about how we arrived there—if you can, at least. Texas saved its season for another week. Period.

But the questions regarding Manning's future will persist. A two-interception game, no matter how good some of the throws for, won't derail the possibility of him ultimately losing his starting job.

That possibility remains a rough 10 minutes away from finally unfolding. And the possibility of Manning playing for a different program next year remains a realistic (and perhaps likely) scenario.

As for Sarkisian, a similar sentiment applies. His contributions to the program have been enormous. He's lifted Texas up from the depths of mediocrity to something much more fitting to a program this grand. Still, the questions surrounding his ability to lift Texas to that next, next level still linger.

Even in a win, a hugely important, had-to-have win for all parties involved, one can't help but feel a sense of uncertainty. The relief was palpable and necessary, although the apprehension to believe that all is finally well has never been greater.

articles.title: Raleek Brown helps No. 19 Texas Longhorns avoid a devastating loss against No. 7 Ole Miss
articles.summary: Arch Manning scored with 8:04 left, and Texas avoided a complete collapse in a 34-27 win over No. 7 Ole Miss. With the win at Royal-Memorial Stadium, No. 19...
articles.body:
Needing a win to keep its College Football Playoff hopes alive, the Texas Longhorns managed to secure one Saturday night.

Texas held off an Ole Miss rally and avoided a complete collapse in the second half of a 34-27 win over No. 7 Ole Miss . With the win at Royal-Memorial Stadium, No. 19 Texas (5-2, 2-2) snapped a two-game losing streak.

Saturday's victory was also UT's second over a top-10 opponent this season.

Leading the Longhorns to a victory was running back Raleek Brown, who rushed for 157 yards, and Ryan Wingo, who had 111 receiving yards. The UT defense also intercepted three passes that were thrown by Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who entered the game as a Heisman Trophy contender, with the last of those turnovers being recorded on the game's final snap.

Behind Arch Manning, Texas seizes another double-digit lead

After Ole Miss went 3-and-out on its first drive, the two teams traded field goals. Then things got weird. During a four-play sequence in the first quarter, the following headlines and highlights took place:

Texas offensive lineman Trevor Goosby suffered an apparent leg injury and was carted off the field.

Arch Manning was intercepted by Ole Miss cornerback Jalyn Crawford.

Trinidad Chambliss was intercepted by UT linebacker Justin Cryer.

Texas receiver Cam Coleman dropped what should have been a 59-yard touchdown.

Thanks to a 2-yard touchdown run by Manning – the quarterback's first rushing score of the season – Texas exited the opening frame with a 10-3 lead. The Longhorns then returned to the end zone in the opening minutes of the second quarter during a touchdown drive that featured Manning rushing for 19 yards on a 3rd-and-17 attempt and Ryan Wingo hauling in a 50-yard toss.

By the end of the first half, Texas had added sophomore running back Michael Terry III's first career touchdown run to the box score and had linebacker Rasheem Biles intercept a 4th-and-goal pass near the goal line in the waning minutes. Those two plays gave UT its largest halftime lead over a ranked opponent since the Longhorns also held a 24-3 edge halfway through their 2024 trip to Michigan.

Ole Miss keeps Texas on its heels, but Longhorns survive

Over its past two losses against Oklahoma and Florida, Texas had built 17-7 and 17-3 leads before spoiling both double-digit advantages. So a sold-out crowd at Royal-Memorial Stadium likely didn't feel much relief at halftime despite the Longhorns' 21-point lead.

And it didn't take long for the Rebels to make those fans sweat.

Ole Miss took advantage of Goosby's absence as Blake Purchase blew past Andre Cojoe on the left side of UT's offensive line to sack Manning and force a fumble that the Rebels recovered for a touchdown. Chambliss then threw a 6-yard touchdown pass to make it a 24-17 game with 6:46 left in the third quarter.

Ole Miss outscored Texas by 14 points in the third quarter and held the Longhorns to 19 yards of offense. To open the fourth quarter, Chambliss then threw a 27-yard touchdown pass to Horatio Fields to tie the game.

But Texas finally found a spark on offense in the fourth quarter as Texas put together a six-play, 80-yard drive that consisted of all runs and was capped by Manning's 1-yard run on a bootleg. Although Manning got his second touchdown of the day, the biggest plays on that drive were Brown's 47-yard sprint through the Ole Miss defense and a 19-yard gain by Terry.

Texas blocked an Ole Miss field goal on the following drive, and then added Gianni Spetic's 33-yard kick on the other end . The Rebels had one more rally in them, however, and Ole Miss kicked a field goal and then recovered an onside kick in the final minutes. But after Ole Miss drove to UT's 24-yard-line with nine seconds left, Chambliss threw two incomplete passes before Jelani McDonald intercepted an end-zone heave to end the game.

Longhorns to continue homestand next week against Mississippi State

While attempting to build off any momentum that it seized on Saturday night, Texas will return to Royal-Memorial Stadium next weekend for its third straight home game. Mississippi State will be the Longhorns' guest on Halloween night.

This season, Mississippi State is 4-3 with a 2-3 mark in SEC play. The Bulldogs are coming off a 23-15 loss to Oklahoma this weekend.

Texas owns a 4-2 lead in an all-time series with Mississippi State that dates back to 1921. The Longhorns have beaten Mississippi State in each of the past two seasons, but Texas had to rally to an overtime win in Starkville last year .
